groups_observed.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core

rules.rule: IP ranges exist in network CIs with no matching discovery schedule (coverage gap)
rules.what_it_means: Subnets derived from network CI data have no corresponding range on any active discovery schedule. Infrastructure exists that discovery has never been told to look for.
rules.why_it_matters: A structural blind spot rather than a failure. Discovery reports success because it completed everything it was asked to do. The CIs in those ranges are either absent or maintained only by integration.
rules.source_tables_fields: Network CI IP data, discovery_schedule, IP range and range-item tables
rules.detection_logic: CIDR set derived from network CIs and router interface data MINUS CIDR set covered by active schedule ranges
rules.threshold_parameter: CIDR overlap analysis, not string matching. Report by subnet with device count.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on range arithmetic. Confidence in the device-count estimate depends on topology data completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Uncovered subnets, estimated device count in each, the device types indicated, and the nearest existing range.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ranges deliberately out of scope: DMZ, third-party managed, OT networks. Maintain a documented exclusion list before raising as Systemic.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — schedule creation is an ITOM change decision
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB-071 and CMDB-070; the CMDB-side view of the same gap

rules.rule: Discovery coverage ratio below threshold — devices found vs. devices expected from topology
rules.what_it_means: The ratio of devices successfully discovered to devices expected, where expected is derived from IP range size, network topology and known infrastructure counts.
rules.why_it_matters: Answers whether discovery is seeing the estate at all. A CMDB health score of 78 computed over 55% of the infrastructure is not a health score.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history, discovery_schedule ranges, network CI topology, ARP and routing data where available
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(distinct devices reaching full classification) / COUNT(devices expected from range and topology derivation)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 85%. The expected-count derivation must be shown alongside the ratio.
rules.confidence_basis: Ratio is exact. Confidence in the denominator depends on the derivation method — state it explicitly and never present the ratio without it.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ratio, the derivation method, ranges ranked by gap size, and the failure phase for each gap.
rules.false_positive_guard: Expected-count derivation over-counts on ranges with heavy DHCP churn or reserved-but-unused address space.
rules.cross_domain_link: Determines the validity of every CMDB freshness metric

rules.rule: No discovery schedule exists for a datacentre or region present in CMDB
rules.what_it_means: A datacentre or region is represented in CMDB location data but has no discovery schedule targeting it.
rules.why_it_matters: An entire site is unmanaged. Usually happens after an acquisition or a datacentre migration where the location records were created and the discovery configuration never followed.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmn_location hierarchy, CI location distribution, discovery_schedule location and range assignment
rules.detection_logic: Locations with CI counts above threshold WHERE no active schedule targets a range mapped to that location
rules.threshold_parameter: CI count threshold configurable, default 50
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on schedule absence. Location-to-range mapping confidence depends on ITOM-004 being clean.
rules.evidence_to_show: Location, CI count, CI classes present, staleness distribution, and the absence of a covering schedule.
rules.false_positive_guard: Site managed by a separate ServiceNow instance or a third party with its own feed.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes site-wide CMDB staleness

rules.rule: Location not defined on discovery schedule
rules.what_it_means: The location field on a discovery schedule is empty. Location on the schedule propagates to every CI that schedule discovers.
rules.why_it_matters: One empty field on one record leaves thousands of CIs with no location. That silently breaks incident routing, DR scoping, asset reconciliation and every location-based impact rule. The consequence is wildly disproportionate to how the defect looks on screen.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule.location, CI location population for CIs discovered by that schedule
rules.detection_logic: Active schedules with an empty location field, joined to the count of CIs they have created or updated
rules.threshold_parameter: Any empty location on an active schedule
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field emptiness. The downstream CI count is exact from discovery attribution.
rules.evidence_to_show: The schedule, its ranges, the count of CIs it has discovered with no location, and the routing or DR rules that depend on location for those CIs.
rules.false_positive_guard: Schedules covering multi-site ranges where location is deliberately set per-CI by a pattern instead. Verify the pattern populates it before dismissing.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — schedule correction as update set, then Lane 1 bulk CI location backfill
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct cause of CMDB-020; escalate to Systemic if the schedule covers principal-class ranges

rules.rule: Schedule inactive but never deleted, with its range still live
rules.what_it_means: A discovery schedule has been deactivated but its IP range is still live infrastructure that nothing else covers.
rules.why_it_matters: Coverage was silently withdrawn. Deactivation is usually a temporary troubleshooting step that nobody reversed, and the CIs in that range have been degrading ever since.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule active flag, range coverage analysis, CI staleness in the affected range
rules.detection_logic: Inactive schedules whose ranges are not covered by any other active schedule AND contain CIs with recent task activity
rules.threshold_parameter: Require evidence the range is still live: recent incidents, recent events, or non-stale CIs from another source
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on schedule state. Liveness evidence at 95%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule, deactivation date and user, the range, the CI count, and their staleness distribution since deactivation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Range genuinely decommissioned and the CIs pending retirement.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — reactivation is an ITOM decision
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB-072 in the affected range

rules.rule: Schedule last successful run beyond its own interval
rules.what_it_means: A schedule's last successful run is older than its own configured interval, by more than a tolerance factor.
rules.why_it_matters: The schedule is configured correctly and is not producing. Either it is failing, being cancelled, or the job queue is not reaching it.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule interval and last run, discovery_status completion records
rules.detection_logic: Schedules where (now - last successful completion) exceeds interval x tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 2x interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamp arithmetic. Cause attribution from discovery_status state at 90%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule, interval, last successful run, run history with outcomes, and the CI staleness now accumulating in its range.
rules.false_positive_guard: Schedule paused deliberately during a maintenance or upgrade window.
rules.cross_domain_link: Leading cause of CMDB-072

rules.rule: Schedule interval longer than CI staleness threshold (guaranteed stale data)
rules.what_it_means: The schedule interval is longer than the staleness threshold applied to the CIs it maintains. Even when discovery works perfectly, those CIs are stale by definition.
rules.why_it_matters: A configuration contradiction. The team is measuring against a threshold their own schedule design cannot meet. Remediating the staleness findings is futile until one of the two numbers changes.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule interval, per-class staleness thresholds, CI class distribution in range
rules.detection_logic: Schedules where interval exceeds the staleness threshold of the dominant CI classes in their ranges
rules.threshold_parameter: Class staleness thresholds configurable; compare against the tightest threshold among classes present
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the arithmetic comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule interval, the class staleness thresholds in play, and the CI count that is permanently stale as a result.
rules.false_positive_guard: Staleness threshold set unrealistically tight rather than the interval being too long. Present both numbers and let the customer choose which to change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Makes CMDB-072 unfixable without a config decision

rules.rule: Schedule assigned to a MID with no network route to its range
rules.what_it_means: A schedule is assigned to a MID Server that has no network route to the range it is meant to scan.
rules.why_it_matters: Every run fails at the network layer before authentication is even attempted. Looks like a credential problem in the logs and is not, which sends troubleshooting down the wrong path for weeks.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule MID assignment, ecc_agent host and network data, discovery_device_history error classes
rules.detection_logic: Schedules whose assigned MID shows connection-level failures across the majority of the range, with no successful device in that range from that MID
rules.threshold_parameter: Majority threshold default 90% of range unreachable
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — network-level failure is inferred from error class distribution rather than observed directly.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule, MID, range, failure error class distribution, and any MID that has succeeded against that range historically.
rules.false_positive_guard: Firewall change that is being reverted, or a genuinely new range not yet routed.
rules.cross_domain_link: Presents as a credential failure; misdiagnosis is common

rules.rule: Schedule running against decommissioned or re-allocated ranges
rules.what_it_means: A schedule is scanning ranges that have been decommissioned or reallocated to a different purpose.
rules.why_it_matters: Wasted MID capacity and runtime, longer run durations, and potential discovery of devices that belong to another team or entity. In a shared address space this can be a security concern.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule ranges, CI counts and staleness per range, network CI subnet data
rules.detection_logic: Ranges with zero successful device discoveries over the window AND no corresponding subnet in current network CI data
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 90 days
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — absence of discovery could mean failure rather than decommission. Corroborate with network CI data.
rules.evidence_to_show: Range, last successful discovery in it, current network CI subnet list, and the run time consumed scanning it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Range temporarily empty during a migration.
rules.cross_domain_link: Contributes to ITOM-029 run duration growth

rules.rule: Overlapping ranges across schedules causing duplicate scanning and reclassification churn
rules.what_it_means: Two or more schedules cover overlapping IP ranges, so the same devices are scanned repeatedly, potentially by different patterns or MIDs.
rules.why_it_matters: Wastes capacity and, worse, can cause reclassification churn when two runs classify the same device differently. That churn is a direct cause of attribute loss.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule ranges, CIDR overlap analysis, sys_audit on sys_class_name for devices in the overlap
rules.detection_logic: Schedule range pairs with CIDR overlap, joined to reclassification events for CIs in the overlapping space
rules.threshold_parameter: Any overlap. Escalate where reclassification churn is present in the overlap.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on overlap arithmetic. Churn attribution at 90%.
rules.evidence_to_show: The overlapping schedules, the shared CIDR space, device count in it, and any class-flipping evidence from audit.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate overlap for different device types using different patterns, correctly scoped.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB-026 reclassification churn

rules.rule: Schedule with no MID cluster or failover MID
rules.what_it_means: A schedule is assigned to a single MID Server with no cluster and no failover MID.
rules.why_it_matters: One MID failure withdraws discovery coverage from that range entirely, and nothing alerts on it. The failure is silent because the schedule reports no error, it simply produces nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule MID assignment, MID cluster configuration
rules.detection_logic: Schedules assigned to a single MID that is not a member of a cluster
rules.threshold_parameter: Escalate where the range contains CIs supporting Business Critical services
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule, MID, cluster membership, range criticality, and the CI count at risk.
rules.false_positive_guard: Small or non-critical ranges where single-MID coverage is a deliberate cost decision.
rules.cross_domain_link: Single point of failure for the covered range

rules.rule: Shazzam batch size or concurrency tuned beyond safe limits for the MID
rules.what_it_means: Shazzam batch size or concurrency is tuned above what the assigned MID host can sustain.
rules.why_it_matters: Produces timeouts and partial runs that look like device problems. The devices are fine; the MID is being asked to do more than it can, and the resulting errors are attributed to the wrong cause.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule batch and concurrency settings, ecc_agent host resource indicators, timeout error distribution
rules.detection_logic: Schedules whose concurrency settings exceed the MID's capability profile, correlated with timeout error clusters
rules.threshold_parameter: Capability profile derived from MID host specification where available; otherwise from observed throughput
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — resource limits are inferred from observed behaviour rather than measured directly.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule settings, MID host profile, timeout error distribution by run, and throughput trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Timeouts caused by slow devices rather than MID saturation. Check whether timeouts cluster by MID or by device type.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM-034 and ITOM-033

rules.rule: Schedule window colliding with backup or change-freeze window
rules.what_it_means: The discovery window overlaps a backup window, change freeze, or other period when scanning is undesirable.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery competes for resource with backup, or scans a device mid-change and records a transient state as truth. Lower severity because the consequence is intermittent.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule run window, cmn_schedule, change blackout and maintenance window definitions
rules.detection_logic: Schedule windows overlapping defined backup, blackout or maintenance windows
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires the customer's schedules to be defined; report the absence if they are not
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on window arithmetic where schedules are defined.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule window, the conflicting window, the overlap duration, and any correlation with run failures.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate scheduling to a quiet period that happens to coincide.
rules.cross_domain_link: Interacts with change calendar awareness

rules.rule: Schedule with no owner or description
rules.what_it_means: A discovery schedule has no owner and no description.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody knows why it exists or who to ask. Becomes a problem only when something needs changing, which is why it is Low, but it is the reason decommissioned schedules survive for years.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_schedule owner and description fields
rules.detection_logic: Active schedules with empty owner AND empty description
rules.threshold_parameter: Both fields empty
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule list with creation date, creating user, and the ranges each covers.
rules.false_positive_guard: Naming convention carries the meaning and the estate does not use the description field.
rules.cross_domain_link: Governance hygiene

rules.rule: Credential failure rate above threshold on a range for N consecutive days
rules.what_it_means: A credential has failed authentication on a range at a rate above threshold, sustained across consecutive days.
rules.why_it_matters: Sustained is the key word. A one-day failure is an incident; a thirty-one-day failure is a governance failure, because it means nobody is reading discovery output. This is the finding that explained the entire router outage.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history authentication outcomes, discovery_credentials, discovery_log error classes
rules.detection_logic: Per credential per range: failure count / attempt count per day, flagged where the ratio exceeds threshold for N consecutive days
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 70% failure rate sustained for 3 consecutive days. Escalate at 14 and 30 days.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the failure ratio. Duration is exact. Escalate severity by duration band — this is the modifier that took the router case from Critical to Systemic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential, range, daily failure ratio trend, the consistent error class, the credential's last update timestamp, and the downstream CI staleness and relationship loss attributable to it.
rules.false_positive_guard: A range where the credential was never intended to apply and correctly fails. Check applies-to scoping before raising.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — SAOS never holds passwords; produce the change record and the targeted rediscovery trigger afterwards
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of CMDB-072, CMDB-056, and downstream impact-analysis blindness

rules.rule: No credential of the required type exists for a range containing devices of that type
rules.what_it_means: A range contains devices of a given type but no credential of the matching type exists or is scoped to that range.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery will never classify those devices. Not a failure, a structural absence — the ladder has no rung for them.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials by type and applies-to scope, device type distribution per range from classification attempts
rules.detection_logic: Ranges where classification attempts indicate a device type with no matching credential type in scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Device type inference from port signature and partial classification
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — device type inference from partial classification is strong but not certain.
rules.evidence_to_show: Range, the device types detected, the credential types in scope, and the classification phase where those devices halt.
rules.false_positive_guard: Devices deliberately excluded from credentialed discovery.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes permanent classification failure in that range

rules.rule: Credential authentication failing (the rotation case)
rules.what_it_means: A credential is failing authentication, typically because the underlying account password or community string was rotated and the ServiceNow credential record was not updated.
rules.why_it_matters: The single most common cause of estate-wide CMDB decay. Silent, because discovery continues to run and report completion while producing nothing for the affected devices.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials last update timestamp, discovery_device_history authentication failures, credential affinity records
rules.detection_logic: Credentials with authentication failures, correlated against the credential record's sys_updated_on to establish the rotation hypothesis
rules.threshold_parameter: Any sustained failure. Temporal correlation with the credential update timestamp strengthens the root-cause claim.
rules.confidence_basis: 98% where three signals align: uniform failure across the range, consistent error class, and failure onset matching the credential update date.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential record with last-update date, failure onset date, affected device count, error class distribution, and the control group of devices still succeeding on a different credential.
rules.false_positive_guard: Account locked or disabled upstream rather than rotated. Same remediation path, different root cause statement.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — guided correction, then triggered rediscovery of the affected range only
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of the router demo chain

rules.rule: Credential expired or inactive but still referenced by a schedule
rules.what_it_means: A credential is expired or set inactive but is still referenced by an active discovery schedule.
rules.why_it_matters: Configuration that looks intact. The schedule has a credential assigned, so the config screen reads correctly, and the credential cannot possibly work.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials active flag and expiry, schedule credential references
rules.detection_logic: Active schedules referencing credentials where active=false or expiry date has passed
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on credential state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential, its state and expiry, the schedules referencing it, and the ranges affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential deactivated as part of a planned rotation with a replacement already in the ladder.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM-017 symptoms

rules.rule: Credential affinity absent for a range, so every run re-tries the full ladder
rules.what_it_means: No credential affinity records exist for a range, so every discovery run retries the full credential ladder against every device.
rules.why_it_matters: Multiplies run duration and authentication load. On a large range this alone can push a run past its window, and it generates failed authentication attempts that can trigger account lockout upstream.
rules.source_tables_fields: Credential affinity records, discovery_credentials ladder depth, range device counts
rules.detection_logic: Ranges with successful discoveries but zero affinity records, or affinity coverage below threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Affinity coverage threshold default 80% of successfully discovered devices
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on affinity record absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Range, device count, ladder depth, affinity record count, and the resulting authentication attempt volume per run.
rules.false_positive_guard: Affinity deliberately disabled, or recently cleared after a credential change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Contributes to ITOM-029 and ITOM-033

rules.rule: Credential with zero successful uses since creation
rules.what_it_means: A credential exists and has never successfully authenticated against anything since it was created.
rules.why_it_matters: Either it was never correct, or it was created for infrastructure that never arrived. It sits in the ladder consuming an attempt against every device, forever.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials creation date, credential success counts from device history
rules.detection_logic: Credentials with zero successful uses and age above threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 90 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on success count.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential, creation date and user, attempt count, and the ranges it is scoped to.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential provisioned ahead of infrastructure that is not yet deployed.
rules.cross_domain_link: Ladder bloat; contributes to run duration

rules.rule: Credential order causing high-privilege credentials to be tried first
rules.what_it_means: The credential ladder is ordered so that high-privilege credentials are attempted before lower-privilege ones.
rules.why_it_matters: Every device sees the privileged credential first. If any device on the range is compromised or logging aggressively, the highest-value credential is the one most exposed. A security finding dressed as a configuration preference.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials order field, credential privilege classification
rules.detection_logic: Credential ladders where a higher-privilege credential has lower order than a lower-privilege credential covering the same devices
rules.threshold_parameter: Privilege classification configurable; derive from the credential's account role where available
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — privilege classification depends on knowledge of the underlying account, which SAOS infers.
rules.evidence_to_show: Ladder order, credential privilege classification, and the device count each is attempted against.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ordering chosen deliberately because the privileged credential is the only one that works on most devices.
rules.cross_domain_link: Security exposure; routes to the security reviewer, not the platform team

rules.rule: Single credential scoped far wider than necessary (blast radius on compromise)
rules.what_it_means: A single credential is scoped to a far wider range than the devices it actually authenticates against.
rules.why_it_matters: Unnecessary blast radius. If that credential is compromised, its stated scope is what an attacker learns it can reach. Least privilege applied to discovery.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials applies-to scope, actual successful authentication distribution
rules.detection_logic: Credentials whose scoped range size substantially exceeds the address space where they actually succeed
rules.threshold_parameter: Ratio threshold configurable, default scope 5x actual success footprint
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the scope-versus-usage comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential, scoped ranges, ranges where it actually succeeds, and the proposed narrowed scope.
rules.false_positive_guard: Scope deliberately broad to accommodate planned expansion.
rules.cross_domain_link: Security exposure

rules.rule: Credential type mismatched to the devices in range (SSH credential on a Windows range)
rules.what_it_means: Credential type does not match the device types present in the range: an SSH credential scoped to a Windows range, an SNMP v2 credential on devices requiring v3.
rules.why_it_matters: Guaranteed authentication failures that look like credential problems rather than scoping problems, so troubleshooting resets the wrong credential.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials type and scope, device type distribution per range
rules.detection_logic: Credential type versus dominant device type per range, flagged where mismatched
rules.threshold_parameter: Device type from successful classification or port signature
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — device type inference from partial classification.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential type, range, device type distribution, and the failure pattern that results.
rules.false_positive_guard: Mixed-type range where multiple credential types are correctly present and one is expected to fail on some devices.
rules.cross_domain_link: Generates noise in ITOM-015 failure ratios

rules.rule: Credential stored outside the credential vault or with vault integration disabled
rules.what_it_means: Credentials are stored outside the credential vault, or vault integration is configured and disabled.
rules.why_it_matters: Secrets sit in the ServiceNow credential table rather than in a managed vault. For a regulated entity this is a control finding with audit consequence, independent of whether discovery works.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials vault integration configuration, external credential store registration
rules.detection_logic: Credentials with no vault reference where vault integration is licensed or configured
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only where a vault capability exists on the instance
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential count stored locally, the vault integration state, and the credential types affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Organisation has no vault and does not intend to deploy one. Report as a control gap rather than a misconfiguration.
rules.cross_domain_link: Security and regulatory finding; feeds the Regulatory Evidence Pack

rules.rule: Credential last updated beyond the organisation's rotation policy
rules.what_it_means: A credential has not been updated within the organisation's stated rotation policy period.
rules.why_it_matters: Policy non-adherence rather than operational failure. Matters for audit and as a leading indicator: an un-rotated credential will eventually be rotated upstream without ServiceNow being told, which produces ITOM-017.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials sys_updated_on, rotation policy period
rules.detection_logic: Credentials whose last update exceeds the policy rotation period
rules.threshold_parameter: Rotation period from the customer's policy, not assumed. Report the absence of a policy separately.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on date arithmetic where a policy period is supplied.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential list with last update date, policy period, and days overdue.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential type not subject to the rotation policy.
rules.cross_domain_link: Predicts future ITOM-017 occurrences

rules.rule: Credential with no applies-to restriction
rules.what_it_means: A credential has no applies-to restriction, so it is attempted against every device in every range.
rules.why_it_matters: Maximum blast radius and maximum wasted authentication attempts. The default state that nobody tightens after implementation.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials applies-to field
rules.detection_logic: Credentials with empty applies-to or a scope covering all ranges
rules.threshold_parameter: Any unrestricted credential
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential list, the total address space they are attempted against, and where they actually succeed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Small estates where a single credential genuinely applies everywhere.
rules.cross_domain_link: Security and performance

rules.rule: Unused credentials never cleaned up
rules.what_it_means: Credentials exist that are not referenced by any active schedule and have no recent successful use.
rules.why_it_matters: Housekeeping. Adds ladder depth and audit surface with no function. Deliberately Low.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_credentials, schedule references, success history
rules.detection_logic: Credentials with no schedule reference AND no successful use in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 180 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on reference and usage absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential list with creation date, last use, and referencing schedules.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential retained for a seasonal or ad-hoc discovery need.
rules.cross_domain_link: Hygiene

rules.rule: Percentage of devices completing full classification below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of devices reaching full classification, as opposed to halting at port scan, classification or exploration.
rules.why_it_matters: The truest measure of whether discovery is working. A run that completes with 40% of devices stuck at port scan is reported as a successful run.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history phase outcomes
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(devices reaching exploration complete) / COUNT(devices detected) per range per run
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 85%. Report by range and by phase.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the phase data.
rules.evidence_to_show: Completion funnel by phase, per range, with the drop-off at each stage and the dominant error class at the largest drop.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ranges containing many devices that are legitimately unclassifiable (IoT, appliances with no agent or SNMP).
rules.cross_domain_link: The execution-side headline; explains CMDB-070

rules.rule: Discovery run duration growing run over run (approaching window overrun)
rules.what_it_means: Discovery run duration is growing run over run, trending toward exceeding its window.
rules.why_it_matters: A slow-motion failure. Nothing breaks until the day a run does not finish, and then coverage drops with no configuration change to point at. Predictable and therefore preventable.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_status start and end timestamps across runs, schedule window definition
rules.detection_logic: Per schedule: run duration trend across the window, projected against the configured window length
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires at least 5 runs. Flag on positive trend with projected overrun within 90 days.
rules.confidence_basis: Trend confidence from run count and variance. State the projection method.
rules.evidence_to_show: Duration trend chart per schedule, the window length, projected overrun date, and the phase consuming the growth.
rules.false_positive_guard: Range genuinely growing in device count. Normalise duration by device count before flagging.
rules.cross_domain_link: Predicts ITOM-033

rules.rule: Devices halting at port-scan phase, never classified
rules.what_it_means: Devices are detected at the port scan phase and never progress to classification.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery can see them and cannot identify them. Usually a credential, port or protocol gap. These devices exist on the network and not in the CMDB.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history phase and outcome
rules.detection_logic: Devices whose furthest phase is port scan, grouped by range and by open port signature
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by range and by port signature to identify the device family
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on phase data. Device family inference from port signature at 85%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Device count by range, open port signatures, inferred device family, and the credential types in scope for that range.
rules.false_positive_guard: Devices deliberately excluded from classification.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB absence rather than staleness

rules.rule: Devices classified but never explored
rules.what_it_means: Devices are classified but exploration never completes, so the CI is created with minimal attributes and no relationships.
rules.why_it_matters: Produces the worst kind of CI: present, so it looks like coverage, and empty, so it carries no relationships and contributes nothing to impact analysis. Directly produces the zero-relationship CIs behind the router failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history phase outcomes, resulting CI attribute and relationship counts
rules.detection_logic: Devices reaching classification but not exploration, joined to the attribute and edge counts on the CIs they produced
rules.threshold_parameter: Report with the resulting CI quality, not just the phase count
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on phase data.
rules.evidence_to_show: Device count, the CIs produced, their attribute completeness and edge counts, and the exploration error class.
rules.false_positive_guard: Device types where exploration is not supported.
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct cause of CMDB-058 zero-relationship CIs

rules.rule: Run completing with error count above threshold
rules.what_it_means: A discovery run completes but with an error count above threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: The run reports success. The completion state is the thing people look at, and it is green. The errors are in a log nobody reads, which is precisely how a 31-day credential failure survives.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_status error counts, discovery_log by error class
rules.detection_logic: Runs whose error count exceeds threshold relative to device count
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 10% of devices producing errors
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on counts.
rules.evidence_to_show: Run, completion state, error count and ratio, error class distribution, and the same figures for previous runs.
rules.false_positive_guard: A one-off burst from a transient network event.
rules.cross_domain_link: The gap between reported success and actual outcome

rules.rule: Run not completing within its window
rules.what_it_means: A discovery run does not complete within its configured window and is truncated or cancelled.
rules.why_it_matters: Partial coverage with no indication of which devices were missed. Every truncated run leaves a different subset stale, so the staleness pattern looks random and is not.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_status start, end and completion state, schedule window
rules.detection_logic: Runs whose end state is cancelled or truncated, or whose duration exceeded the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report frequency
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on run state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Run history with completion states, the devices reached versus expected per run, and the accumulating staleness.
rules.false_positive_guard: Run cancelled deliberately.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes intermittent, hard-to-diagnose staleness

rules.rule: Timeouts clustered on a specific MID or subnet
rules.what_it_means: Timeout errors cluster on a specific MID Server or a specific subnet rather than distributing evenly.
rules.why_it_matters: Clustering is the diagnostic. Even distribution suggests device-side slowness; clustering on one MID suggests MID saturation, and clustering on one subnet suggests a network path problem.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history timeout errors by MID and by subnet
rules.detection_logic: Timeout distribution by MID and by subnet, flagged where one dimension holds a disproportionate share
rules.threshold_parameter: Disproportion threshold default 3x expected share
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on distribution. The causal interpretation is stated as a hypothesis.
rules.evidence_to_show: Timeout distribution by MID and by subnet, with the expected share for comparison, and the MID resource indicators for the implicated MID.
rules.false_positive_guard: A subnet genuinely containing slow devices.
rules.cross_domain_link: Distinguishes MID capacity from network path problems

rules.rule: Devices discovered but producing no CI (sensor failure)
rules.what_it_means: Devices are successfully discovered and explored but no CI is produced, indicating a sensor or transform failure.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery did all the work and the output was dropped. Highly diagnostic, because the failure is in a narrow and fixable place.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history successful outcomes, CI creation attribution from those runs
rules.detection_logic: Devices completing exploration with no corresponding CI create or update in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Correlate by device identity and run timestamp
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — CI attribution to a specific discovery run depends on audit completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Device count, the successful run records, the absent CI records, and any sensor script errors in the log for that run.
rules.false_positive_guard: CI created but immediately merged by IRE into an existing record. Check for IRE merge events before flagging.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB absence despite successful discovery

rules.rule: ECC queue input backlog beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: The ECC queue input backlog exceeds threshold — results are arriving faster than the instance can process them.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery output is queued, not applied. The CMDB lags reality by the length of the backlog, and nothing in the discovery reporting indicates it.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_queue aggregated by state, topic and age
rules.detection_logic: Input queue depth and oldest-record age, against threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Depth and age thresholds configurable; age is the more meaningful of the two
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on queue aggregates.
rules.evidence_to_show: Queue depth trend, oldest record age, topic distribution, and the processing rate versus arrival rate.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient backlog during a large scheduled run.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CMDB lag independent of discovery success

rules.rule: ECC queue output processing lag
rules.what_it_means: The ECC output queue is processing with lag — instructions to MIDs are queued rather than dispatched.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery work does not start when scheduled. Runs appear to take longer when they are actually waiting to begin, which sends tuning effort in the wrong direction.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_queue output state aggregates, MID pickup timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Output queue records with dispatch lag above threshold, by MID
rules.threshold_parameter: Lag threshold configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on queue timestamps.
rules.evidence_to_show: Lag distribution by MID, queue depth trend, and MID availability during the lag periods.
rules.false_positive_guard: MID deliberately offline during a window.
rules.cross_domain_link: Inflates apparent run duration

rules.rule: Discovery log error volume trending up
rules.what_it_means: Discovery log error volume is trending upward across runs.
rules.why_it_matters: A leading indicator with no single attributable cause. Useful for early detection and for demonstrating that something changed, even before the specific rule that catches it fires.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_log error counts by class across runs
rules.detection_logic: Error volume trend by class across the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires at least 5 runs
rules.confidence_basis: Trend confidence from run count and variance.
rules.evidence_to_show: Error volume trend by class, with the classes contributing most to the growth.
rules.false_positive_guard: Log verbosity increased, changing the baseline. Check for a logging configuration change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Early warning across the ITOM domain

rules.rule: Runs cancelled manually and never re-run
rules.what_it_means: Discovery runs have been cancelled manually and never re-run.
rules.why_it_matters: Each cancellation leaves a coverage gap that nothing closes. Often done during an incident and forgotten afterwards.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_status cancellation records and user, subsequent run history
rules.detection_logic: Cancelled runs with no successful completion of the same schedule afterwards within the interval
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on run state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Cancellation record with user and timestamp, the affected range, and the staleness accumulated since.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cancellation followed by a successful ad-hoc run not linked to the schedule.
rules.cross_domain_link: Produces range-specific coverage gaps

rules.rule: Discovery status records accumulating without cleanup
rules.what_it_means: discovery_status and related run history records are accumulating with no cleanup or rotation configured.
rules.why_it_matters: Table growth and slower queries against discovery history. Low severity, real at scale, and easy to fix.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_status row counts and growth, rotation configuration
rules.detection_logic: Discovery history table sizes and growth rate, against rotation configuration state
rules.threshold_parameter: Size threshold configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on counts and configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Table sizes, growth rate, oldest record, and rotation configuration state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Retention required for audit over a longer period than default.
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds platform scale findings

rules.rule: Custom pattern overriding OOB with lower success rate
rules.what_it_means: A custom pattern overrides an out-of-box pattern and achieves a lower success rate than the OOB pattern it replaced.
rules.why_it_matters: The customisation made things worse and nobody measured it. Also creates upgrade risk, since the custom pattern will not receive the improvements ServiceNow ships.
rules.source_tables_fields: sa_pattern custom and OOB versions, pattern execution success rates by device class
rules.detection_logic: Custom patterns overriding an OOB pattern, compared on success rate against the same device class
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires sufficient execution volume on both; default minimum 50 executions
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the success rate comparison where volume is sufficient. State the volume.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both patterns, their success rates, execution volumes, device class, and the failure classes for the custom pattern.
rules.false_positive_guard: Custom pattern covers a device variant the OOB pattern cannot handle, so a lower aggregate rate is expected. Compare like device subsets.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — reverting a pattern is an architecture decision
rules.cross_domain_link: Upgrade risk plus discovery quality

rules.rule: Pattern with zero successful executions in the window
rules.what_it_means: A pattern has zero successful executions in the observation window.
rules.why_it_matters: It runs and never works, or it never runs. Either way it contributes nothing and consumes execution time.
rules.source_tables_fields: sa_pattern execution results
rules.detection_logic: Patterns with zero successful executions and at least one attempt in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 90 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on execution records.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern, attempt count, failure classes, the device classes it targets, and the schedules invoking it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Pattern for infrastructure not currently present in the estate.
rules.cross_domain_link: Silent discovery gap for the targeted device class

rules.rule: Pattern failing repeatedly on the same device class
rules.what_it_means: A pattern fails repeatedly against the same device class, while succeeding elsewhere.
rules.why_it_matters: Narrows the problem to a pattern-plus-device-class combination, which is precisely fixable. The affected device class is being under-discovered while everything else looks fine.
rules.source_tables_fields: Pattern execution results grouped by pattern and device class
rules.detection_logic: Pattern and device class pairs with failure rate above threshold, where the pattern succeeds on other classes
rules.threshold_parameter: Failure rate threshold default 60% with minimum volume 20
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the grouped failure rate.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern, device class, failure rate, the failing step, and the success rate on other classes for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: Device class genuinely unsupported by the pattern and covered by another.
rules.cross_domain_link: Class-specific discovery gap

rules.rule: Pattern steps timing out consistently
rules.what_it_means: Specific pattern steps time out consistently across executions.
rules.why_it_matters: Identifies the exact step to fix rather than declaring the pattern broken. Often a single command or query against a device type that responds slowly.
rules.source_tables_fields: Pattern step execution results and durations
rules.detection_logic: Pattern steps with timeout rate above threshold across executions
rules.threshold_parameter: Timeout rate threshold default 30% with minimum volume 20
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on step-level results where step data is retained.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern, step, timeout rate, average duration of successful executions of that step, and the device classes affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Step timing out against a small number of genuinely slow devices.
rules.cross_domain_link: Contributes to ITOM-031 incomplete exploration

rules.rule: Deprecated probes still referenced by active schedules
rules.what_it_means: Deprecated probes are still referenced by active discovery schedules.
rules.why_it_matters: Deprecated components are not maintained and may stop working at any upgrade. Running on them is borrowed time, and the failure when it comes will be attributed to the upgrade.
rules.source_tables_fields: Probe definitions with deprecation markers, schedule and pattern references
rules.detection_logic: Active schedules or patterns referencing probes marked deprecated in the current instance version
rules.threshold_parameter: Deprecation status from the instance's own metadata
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on deprecation markers where present.
rules.evidence_to_show: Probe, deprecation status, referencing schedules and patterns, and the recommended replacement.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deprecated probe still functional and no replacement available.
rules.cross_domain_link: Upgrade risk

rules.rule: Pattern version behind the instance version after upgrade
rules.what_it_means: Pattern versions are behind the instance version following an upgrade.
rules.why_it_matters: Upgrades ship pattern improvements. Running old patterns on a new instance means discovery quality did not improve with the upgrade, and may have regressed if the platform changed underneath.
rules.source_tables_fields: sa_pattern versions, instance version, ServiceNow shipped pattern versions
rules.detection_logic: Patterns whose version predates the current instance family
rules.threshold_parameter: Compare against the pattern version shipped with the current family
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on version comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern list with current and shipped versions, and success rate before and after the upgrade.
rules.false_positive_guard: Pattern deliberately pinned because a later version regressed for this estate.
rules.cross_domain_link: Post-upgrade discovery quality

rules.rule: Custom pattern with no version control or documentation
rules.what_it_means: Custom patterns exist with no version control reference, no documentation and no owner.
rules.why_it_matters: Unmaintainable. When it breaks, nobody knows what it was supposed to do or who built it, and the usual outcome is a rewrite.
rules.source_tables_fields: sa_pattern custom flag, description, owner, update set lineage
rules.detection_logic: Custom patterns with empty description AND no owner AND no update set lineage
rules.threshold_parameter: All three absent
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern list with creation date, creating user, device classes targeted, and execution volume.
rules.false_positive_guard: Documentation held externally with a naming reference.
rules.cross_domain_link: Maintainability and key-person risk

rules.rule: Pattern producing CIs that IRE then duplicates
rules.what_it_means: A pattern produces CIs that the identification engine subsequently treats as duplicates of existing records.
rules.why_it_matters: The pattern and the identification rules disagree about what identifies a device. Produces a steady stream of duplicates with a single fixable cause, and remediating the duplicates without fixing the pattern is endless.
rules.source_tables_fields: Pattern CI creation attribution, IRE duplicate and error records, duplicate set membership by creating pattern
rules.detection_logic: Duplicate sets whose members were created by a specific pattern, ranked by pattern
rules.threshold_parameter: Minimum duplicate count per pattern configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — creation attribution to a specific pattern depends on audit completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern, duplicate count attributable to it, the identity attributes it populates versus those the identification rule requires, and sample duplicate sets.
rules.false_positive_guard: Duplicates caused by the identification rule rather than the pattern. Present both and let the evidence decide.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — pattern or identification rule correction
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of a duplicate population; pairs with CMDB-044

rules.rule: Sensor script errors
rules.what_it_means: Sensor scripts are throwing errors during result processing.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery data arrives and fails to land. Similar in effect to ITOM-035 but with an identifiable script to fix.
rules.source_tables_fields: Sensor execution errors in the discovery log, grouped by sensor
rules.detection_logic: Sensors with error counts above threshold in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold relative to execution volume
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on error counts.
rules.evidence_to_show: Sensor, error count and class, sample stack traces, and the device classes affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Errors from a transient data condition.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes CI creation failure after successful discovery

rules.rule: Unused custom patterns never retired
rules.what_it_means: Custom patterns exist that are not referenced by any active schedule and have no recent executions.
rules.why_it_matters: Housekeeping and upgrade surface. Each unused custom pattern is something that must be reviewed at every upgrade for no benefit.
rules.source_tables_fields: sa_pattern custom flag, schedule references, execution history
rules.detection_logic: Custom patterns with no schedule reference AND no execution in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Window default 180 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on reference and execution absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Pattern list with creation date, last execution, and referencing schedules.
rules.false_positive_guard: Pattern retained for an infrastructure type due to be deployed.
rules.cross_domain_link: Upgrade surface reduction

rules.rule: Single MID with no cluster carrying a production-critical range
rules.what_it_means: A single MID Server with no cluster membership carries discovery or integration work for a production-critical range.
rules.why_it_matters: One host failure withdraws visibility from critical infrastructure, and the failure is silent because schedules report no error — they simply produce nothing. The MID is the single most under-protected component in most ITOM deployments.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent records, MID cluster configuration, schedule assignment, range criticality
rules.detection_logic: MIDs not in a cluster that are the sole assignment for ranges containing Business Critical supporting CIs
rules.threshold_parameter: Criticality determined by the services the range's CIs support
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on cluster configuration. Criticality attribution depends on CMDB relationship completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, cluster state, the ranges it solely covers, CI count, and the Business Critical services those CIs support.
rules.false_positive_guard: Range where single-MID coverage is a documented cost decision with accepted risk.
rules.cross_domain_link: Single point of failure; predicts ITOM-153

rules.rule: All MIDs in a cluster on the same host or hypervisor (false redundancy)
rules.what_it_means: All MIDs in a cluster run on the same physical host or hypervisor.
rules.why_it_matters: Redundancy that is not redundant. The cluster passes every configuration check and fails entirely when one host goes down. Worse than no cluster, because the team believes they are protected.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent host data, cluster membership, host CI relationships to hypervisor or physical host
rules.detection_logic: Clusters where all member MIDs resolve to the same host CI or the same hypervisor parent
rules.threshold_parameter: Resolve through the CMDB host relationship where available; otherwise compare host identifiers
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — depends on host CI relationship accuracy, which is itself a CMDB finding.
rules.evidence_to_show: Cluster, member MIDs, their host CIs, the shared parent, and the ranges the cluster covers.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate co-location with a documented DR MID elsewhere.
rules.cross_domain_link: False redundancy; depends on CMDB-059 being correct to detect

rules.rule: MID down or in a degraded state
rules.what_it_means: A MID Server is down or reporting a degraded state.
rules.why_it_matters: Everything assigned to it stops. Discovery, integrations and event connectors that route through it all fail together, which is why a MID outage produces findings across three domains at once.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent status and last refresh, ecc_agent_issue
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with status not Up, or last refresh beyond the heartbeat tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Heartbeat tolerance default 3x expected interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on status and heartbeat.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, status, last refresh, issue records, and the full list of schedules, integrations and connectors assigned to it.
rules.false_positive_guard: MID deliberately stopped during maintenance.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes simultaneous discovery, integration and event failures

rules.rule: MID version behind instance version after upgrade
rules.what_it_means: MID Server version is behind the instance version following an upgrade.
rules.why_it_matters: Version mismatch causes subtle failures rather than clean ones: some probes work, some do not, and the pattern of what breaks is not obvious. Post-upgrade discovery degradation is frequently this.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent version, instance version and family
rules.detection_logic: MIDs whose version does not match the current instance version
rules.threshold_parameter: Compare major and minor version against instance
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on version comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID list with versions, instance version, upgrade date, and discovery success rate before and after the upgrade.
rules.false_positive_guard: MID upgrade in progress with a staged rollout.
rules.cross_domain_link: Post-upgrade discovery degradation

rules.rule: MID validation not completed
rules.what_it_means: MID Server validation has not been completed, so the MID cannot be trusted by the instance for privileged operations.
rules.why_it_matters: Some operations silently do not execute. The MID appears Up and functional and is partially disabled.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent validation status
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with validation status incomplete or not validated
rules.threshold_parameter: Any unvalidated MID in production use
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on validation status.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, validation status, the operations it is assigned, and the operations blocked by non-validation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Newly deployed MID awaiting scheduled validation.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes partial, hard-to-diagnose failures

rules.rule: MID certificate expired or expiring within 30 days
rules.what_it_means: A MID Server certificate has expired or expires within 30 days.
rules.why_it_matters: An expiry is a scheduled outage that nobody has scheduled. Everything the MID carries stops on a known date, and the cause is rarely the first thing anyone checks.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent certificate data, expiry dates
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with certificate expiry in the past or within the warning window
rules.threshold_parameter: Warning window default 30 days. Escalate inside 7 days.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on expiry dates.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, certificate expiry date, days remaining, and everything assigned to the MID that will stop.
rules.false_positive_guard: Certificate renewal already staged and pending deployment.
rules.cross_domain_link: Scheduled future outage across all assigned work

rules.rule: MID capability mismatched to assigned work
rules.what_it_means: A MID's assigned capabilities do not match the work routed to it.
rules.why_it_matters: Work is dispatched to a MID that cannot perform it. Produces failures attributed to the target device rather than to the routing.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent_capability, schedule and integration assignment, work type
rules.detection_logic: MIDs assigned work whose required capability is absent from their capability set
rules.threshold_parameter: Capability requirements per work type
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on capability comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, its capabilities, the assigned work, the required capability, and the resulting failures.
rules.false_positive_guard: Capability implied rather than explicitly declared.
rules.cross_domain_link: Produces misattributed failures

rules.rule: Single MID carrying a disproportionate share of total load
rules.what_it_means: A single MID carries a disproportionate share of total ITOM load relative to its cluster peers.
rules.why_it_matters: Concentration creates a capacity ceiling and a failure concentration. Usually the result of schedules being assigned to a named MID rather than to the cluster.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_queue volume by MID, schedule and integration assignment distribution
rules.detection_logic: Per cluster: work volume by MID, flagged where one holds a disproportionate share
rules.threshold_parameter: Disproportion threshold default 2x the cluster mean
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on volume distribution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Load distribution across the cluster, the assignments causing the concentration, and the resulting queue lag on the loaded MID.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate specialisation where one MID handles a heavy workload by design.
rules.cross_domain_link: Capacity ceiling and failure concentration

rules.rule: MID issue count rising
rules.what_it_means: MID issue count is rising over the observation window.
rules.why_it_matters: Leading indicator of MID degradation before it fails outright. Gives a window to act before the outage.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent_issue counts and trend
rules.detection_logic: Issue count per MID trended across the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires at least 3 observation points
rules.confidence_basis: Trend confidence from window length and variance.
rules.evidence_to_show: Issue count trend per MID with issue type breakdown, and the MID host resource indicators over the same period.
rules.false_positive_guard: A single burst from a network event.
rules.cross_domain_link: Predicts ITOM-053

rules.rule: MID host resource exhaustion indicators (heap, thread, disk)
rules.what_it_means: MID host resource indicators show exhaustion: heap pressure, thread saturation, or disk space depletion.
rules.why_it_matters: The MID is Up and cannot do its work. Produces timeouts and partial runs that are attributed to devices and networks.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent host resource data, issue records referencing resource conditions
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with resource indicators beyond configured limits, or issue records of resource class
rules.threshold_parameter: Thresholds from MID configuration where available
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — resource data availability varies by MID version and configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, resource indicator values and limits, trend, and the timeout or failure rate correlated with the resource condition.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient spike during a large run.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of ITOM-034 timeout clustering

rules.rule: MID last refreshed beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: A MID's last refresh timestamp exceeds the heartbeat tolerance without the status having changed to Down.
rules.why_it_matters: The MID is not communicating and the status has not caught up. A short window where the instance believes it has a working MID that it does not.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent last refresh timestamp, status
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with status Up but last refresh beyond tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 3x heartbeat interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamp arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, status, last refresh, heartbeat interval, and the work dispatched to it since the last refresh.
rules.false_positive_guard: Brief network interruption already recovered.
rules.cross_domain_link: Early signal of ITOM-053

rules.rule: MID with no assigned capabilities but referenced by schedules
rules.what_it_means: A MID has no capabilities assigned but is referenced by schedules or integrations.
rules.why_it_matters: Work is routed to a MID that has declared it can do nothing. Fails immediately and the error rarely names the cause.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent_capability, schedule and integration references
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with zero capability records that are referenced by active schedules or integrations
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on capability and reference data.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, its empty capability set, and the schedules and integrations referencing it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Capability assignment pending on a newly deployed MID.
rules.cross_domain_link: Immediate failure of all assigned work

rules.rule: MID user account over-privileged on the instance side
rules.what_it_means: The MID Server's instance-side user account holds more privilege than the MID's work requires.
rules.why_it_matters: The MID is a network-attached component holding instance credentials. Over-privilege there is a meaningful security exposure, and mid_server plus the specific required roles is almost always sufficient.
rules.source_tables_fields: MID user account roles, required roles for assigned work types
rules.detection_logic: MID user accounts holding roles beyond the required set for their assigned work
rules.threshold_parameter: Required role set per work type; admin on a MID account is always flagged
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on role comparison against the required set.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID user, its roles, the required role set, and the excess roles with what each grants.
rules.false_positive_guard: Broad roles required by a custom integration routed through the MID. Document and except.
rules.cross_domain_link: Security exposure; routes to the security reviewer

rules.rule: MID not on a supported JVM or OS version
rules.what_it_means: The MID host is running an unsupported JVM or operating system version.
rules.why_it_matters: Support and compatibility risk. Becomes acute at upgrade, when the new MID version may not run on the host at all.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent host JVM and OS data, supported version matrix for the instance version
rules.detection_logic: MIDs whose JVM or OS falls outside the supported matrix for the current instance family
rules.threshold_parameter: Supported matrix per instance family
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — depends on the accuracy of host data reported by the MID.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, host JVM and OS versions, the supported matrix, and the upgrade path required.
rules.false_positive_guard: Host scheduled for replacement.
rules.cross_domain_link: Upgrade blocker

rules.rule: MID log rotation not configured
rules.what_it_means: MID log rotation is not configured, so logs grow without bound on the MID host.
rules.why_it_matters: Eventually fills the disk and takes the MID down, producing ITOM-053 with an unobvious cause. Cheap to prevent.
rules.source_tables_fields: MID configuration, host disk indicators
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with no log rotation configuration, joined to disk utilisation trend
rules.threshold_parameter: Any unconfigured MID; escalate where disk utilisation is trending up
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. Disk trend depends on host data availability.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID, rotation configuration state, current log volume, and disk utilisation trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rotation handled by an external host-level process.
rules.cross_domain_link: Preventable cause of ITOM-053

rules.rule: Orphaned MID records for decommissioned hosts
rules.what_it_means: ecc_agent records exist for MID hosts that have been decommissioned.
rules.why_it_matters: Clutter in assignment lists and validation reports. Low consequence, but it makes every MID-related report harder to read and can cause work to be assigned to a MID that does not exist.
rules.source_tables_fields: ecc_agent records with no heartbeat over an extended period, host CI lifecycle
rules.detection_logic: MIDs with no heartbeat beyond threshold AND host CI retired or absent
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold default 90 days with no heartbeat
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on heartbeat absence. Host correlation at 90%.
rules.evidence_to_show: MID list, last heartbeat, host CI state, and any schedules still referencing them.
rules.false_positive_guard: MID temporarily offline for an extended maintenance.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — mark as down or delete, reversible
rules.cross_domain_link: Hygiene

rules.rule: Percentage of Business Critical services with no map at all
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of Business Critical services that have no service map at all.
rules.why_it_matters: The services that matter most are the ones with no dependency model. Impact analysis for them is structurally impossible regardless of how healthy the CMDB is elsewhere.
rules.source_tables_fields: Service map definitions, CSDM service records with criticality
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(Business Critical services with no map) / COUNT(Business Critical services)
rules.threshold_parameter: Any non-zero value is notable. Default threshold 10%.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on map presence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Service list with criticality, incident volume, map presence, and the mapping approach available for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Services legitimately mapped through relationships rather than Service Mapping.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of impact-analysis failure on critical services

rules.rule: Map coverage ratio across the application service estate below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The ratio of application services with a current map to the total application service estate.
rules.why_it_matters: The coverage denominator for Service Mapping. Tells you how much of the service model is evidence-based rather than asserted.
rules.source_tables_fields: Application service records, map definitions and refresh status
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(application services with a current map) / COUNT(application services)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 60%. Current means refreshed within its interval.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidence_to_show: Coverage ratio, unmapped service list ranked by criticality and incident volume, and the mapping approach available.
rules.false_positive_guard: Services deliberately excluded from mapping.
rules.cross_domain_link: Determines the evidence basis for the service model

rules.rule: Maps built manually where automated mapping is available and licensed
rules.what_it_means: Service maps are maintained manually where automated Service Mapping is licensed and capable.
rules.why_it_matters: Manual maps do not self-correct. They are accurate on the day they are built and decay from then on, with nothing to detect the decay. The capability to fix this is already paid for.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map creation method, Service Mapping licensing and pattern availability, entry point feasibility
rules.detection_logic: Manually created maps for services whose technology stack is covered by available mapping patterns
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires Service Mapping licensed and pattern coverage confirmed
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — pattern coverage assessment is an inference about feasibility.
rules.evidence_to_show: Manual map list, service technology stack, the available patterns covering it, and the map's age since last review.
rules.false_positive_guard: Technology stack genuinely not covered by any pattern.
rules.cross_domain_link: Structural cause of map decay

rules.rule: Entry point unreachable or failing
rules.what_it_means: A service map entry point is unreachable or failing.
rules.why_it_matters: Mapping starts at the entry point. If it fails, the entire map for that service stops refreshing, and the existing map silently ages without any indication on the service record.
rules.source_tables_fields: Entry point definitions, mapping run status and errors
rules.detection_logic: Entry points with failure state or no successful traversal in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Window aligned to the map refresh interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on entry point status.
rules.evidence_to_show: Entry point, failure class, last successful traversal, the service affected, and the age of the map it can no longer refresh.
rules.false_positive_guard: Entry point for a service in planned downtime.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM-071 silently

rules.rule: Map last refreshed beyond interval
rules.what_it_means: A service map has not been refreshed within its configured interval.
rules.why_it_matters: The map describes a past state. Every impact calculation using it inherits that lag, and the lag is invisible on the service record.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map refresh timestamps, configured refresh interval
rules.detection_logic: Maps whose last refresh exceeds interval x tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 2x interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamp arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Map, service, last refresh, interval, and the CMDB changes to its CIs since the last refresh.
rules.false_positive_guard: Refresh paused during a change freeze.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes map-versus-CMDB divergence

rules.rule: Map returning fewer CIs than the previous run (silent map collapse)
rules.what_it_means: A map refresh returned substantially fewer CIs than the previous run.
rules.why_it_matters: Silent map collapse. The refresh succeeded, so nothing errors, and the map quietly lost half its topology. Often the first visible symptom of a credential or discovery failure on one tier.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map CI counts across refresh runs
rules.detection_logic: Maps whose CI count dropped by more than threshold between consecutive successful refreshes
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 20% drop. Escalate above 50%.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the count comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Map, CI count history, the CIs lost, the tier they sat in, and the discovery or credential state for that tier.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuine decommissioning of part of the service topology.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — investigate the cause before restoring
rules.cross_domain_link: Symptom of ITOM-015 or ITOM-031 on a specific tier

rules.rule: Map contradicting cmdb\_rel\_ci relationships
rules.what_it_means: The service map asserts relationships that contradict cmdb_rel_ci, or omits relationships the CMDB holds.
rules.why_it_matters: Two sources of truth for the same dependency. Which one a given feature reads determines the answer, and the estate has two answers.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map topology, cmdb_rel_ci for the same CI set
rules.detection_logic: Symmetric difference between map edges and CMDB edges for the mapped CI set
rules.threshold_parameter: Report both directions separately
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on set comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Per service: edges in map only, edges in CMDB only, edges in both, with source and date for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Map deliberately scoped narrower than the full CMDB topology.
rules.cross_domain_link: Consistency defect between the two dependency mechanisms

rules.rule: Application service with an entry point but zero mapped CIs
rules.what_it_means: An application service has a defined entry point but zero mapped CIs.
rules.why_it_matters: Mapping was configured and never produced anything. Looks configured, delivers nothing, and the service record gives no indication.
rules.source_tables_fields: Entry point definitions, map CI associations
rules.detection_logic: Application services with an entry point but zero mapped CI associations
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on association count.
rules.evidence_to_show: Service, entry point, entry point status, mapping run history, and the failure class at the first traversal step.
rules.false_positive_guard: Entry point configured in advance of the first mapping run.
rules.cross_domain_link: Configured-but-empty service model

rules.rule: Map producing CIs that IRE then duplicates
rules.what_it_means: Service Mapping creates CIs that the identification engine subsequently duplicates.
rules.why_it_matters: Mapping and identification disagree about identity. Every map refresh adds duplicates, so the duplicate count grows on a schedule.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map-created CI attribution, IRE duplicate records, duplicate set membership
rules.detection_logic: Duplicate sets whose members were created by a mapping run
rules.threshold_parameter: Minimum count configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — creation attribution depends on audit completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: Duplicate count attributable to mapping, the identity attributes mapping populates versus those identification requires, and sample sets.
rules.false_positive_guard: Duplicates caused by the identification rule rather than mapping.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — identification rule or mapping configuration correction
rules.cross_domain_link: Scheduled duplicate generation; pairs with CMDB-044

rules.rule: Map incomplete — traversal terminating before reaching infrastructure tier
rules.what_it_means: Map traversal terminates before reaching the infrastructure tier, so the map covers application components only.
rules.why_it_matters: The map looks populated and stops above the layer where most failures originate. Infrastructure events never reach the service.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map topology depth and terminal CI classes per service
rules.detection_logic: Maps whose deepest CI class does not reach the infrastructure tier for the estate's own tier model
rules.threshold_parameter: Tier model derived from the best-mapped services in the estate
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on measured depth. Expected depth is derived; state the derivation.
rules.evidence_to_show: Map, its depth, the terminal tier, the expected tier, and the traversal step where it stops.
rules.false_positive_guard: Services with genuinely shallow architecture.
rules.cross_domain_link: Explains why infrastructure events never reach services

rules.rule: Map not reaching the network tier (the router demo gap)
rules.what_it_means: Map traversal does not reach the network tier — no switches, routers or network paths appear in any service map.
rules.why_it_matters: This is the exact gap behind the router outage. Network infrastructure carries every service and appears in none of them, so a network failure returns zero affected services no matter how correct everything else is.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map topology terminal classes, network CI class presence in maps
