rules.detection_logic: Services whose maps contain zero network-class CIs, across the mapped estate
rules.threshold_parameter: Report as an estate-wide ratio, not only per service
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on class presence in maps.
rules.evidence_to_show: Percentage of maps reaching the network tier, the tier at which traversal typically stops, and the network CI population that appears in no map.
rules.false_positive_guard: Network deliberately modelled outside service maps with an alternative impact mechanism.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — structure decision then relationship creation
rules.cross_domain_link: The specific gap that produced the router demo failure

rules.rule: Map with unresolved or unmatched CIs
rules.what_it_means: Mapping produces CIs that cannot be resolved or matched to existing CMDB records.
rules.why_it_matters: Unmatched CIs either become duplicates or are discarded. Both outcomes degrade the map, and neither is visible on the service record.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map run output, unmatched CI records, IRE results
rules.detection_logic: Mapping runs producing unmatched or unresolved CI entries, by service and by class
rules.threshold_parameter: Report count and class distribution
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on unmatched counts where retained.
rules.evidence_to_show: Service, unmatched entry count, the classes affected, and the identity attributes mapping supplied versus those identification required.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient unmatched entries resolved on the next run.
rules.cross_domain_link: Precursor to ITOM-075

rules.rule: Tag-based service definitions with no refresh schedule
rules.what_it_means: Tag-based service definitions have no refresh schedule, so tag changes never propagate into the service model.
rules.why_it_matters: Cloud resources are tagged dynamically and the service model is not updated. The model reflects the tags as they were on the day the definition was created.
rules.source_tables_fields: Tag-based service definitions, refresh schedule configuration
rules.detection_logic: Tag-based definitions with no refresh schedule or with a schedule that has not run within the interval
rules.threshold_parameter: Any unscheduled definition
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on schedule configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Definition, tag criteria, last evaluation, and the resources that currently match versus those in the model.
rules.false_positive_guard: Static tag criteria that genuinely do not change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes cloud service model drift

rules.rule: Manual map with no review since creation
rules.what_it_means: A manually created map has not been reviewed since it was created.
rules.why_it_matters: Manual maps decay from day one with nothing to detect it. An unreviewed manual map on a critical service is an assertion with no evidence behind it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map creation method and date, review or update history
rules.detection_logic: Manual maps with no update or review record since creation, above age threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 365 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on update history absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Map, creation date and user, service criticality, and the CMDB changes to its CIs since creation.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely stable topology.
rules.cross_domain_link: Compounds ITOM-069

rules.rule: Map discovery credentials failing for mapping-specific access
rules.what_it_means: Credentials specific to Service Mapping traversal are failing, distinct from general discovery credentials.
rules.why_it_matters: Mapping requires deeper access than discovery in places. A mapping-specific credential failure produces incomplete maps while general discovery continues to succeed, which makes the cause hard to find.
rules.source_tables_fields: Mapping run credential errors, discovery_credentials scoped to mapping
rules.detection_logic: Mapping runs with authentication failures, grouped by credential and by service
rules.threshold_parameter: Any sustained failure
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — mapping credential attribution from run logs.
rules.evidence_to_show: Credential, affected services, failure rate, the traversal step where it fails, and the general discovery success rate on the same devices for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential correctly failing on devices outside its intended scope.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM-076 and ITOM-072

rules.rule: Entry point defined but no corresponding traffic-based validation
rules.what_it_means: An entry point is defined but there is no traffic-based validation confirming it is the real entry point for the service.
rules.why_it_matters: The map may be traversing from the wrong place, producing a topology that is internally consistent and describes the wrong thing.
rules.source_tables_fields: Entry point definitions, traffic-based connection data where collected
rules.detection_logic: Entry points with no corroborating traffic or connection evidence
rules.threshold_parameter: Only fires where traffic-based data collection is available
rules.confidence_basis: 80% — absence of traffic evidence is weaker than contradicting evidence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Entry point, the traffic data available, and any alternative entry point the traffic suggests.
rules.false_positive_guard: Traffic-based collection not deployed. Report as a capability gap instead.
rules.cross_domain_link: Map correctness rather than completeness

rules.rule: Duplicate application services mapping the same entry point
rules.what_it_means: Two or more application services define the same entry point.
rules.why_it_matters: Both maps traverse the same topology and both claim it. Impact analysis double-counts, and a single failure appears to affect two services when it affects one.
rules.source_tables_fields: Entry point definitions grouped by address and port
rules.detection_logic: Entry point definitions appearing on more than one application service
rules.threshold_parameter: Exact match on address and port
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on exact match.
rules.evidence_to_show: The entry point, the services claiming it, their mapped CI overlap, and their incident histories.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate shared entry point for services that genuinely share infrastructure.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes duplicate service constructs in CSDM

rules.rule: Connector erroring or not run within its interval
rules.what_it_means: An Event Management connector is erroring or has not executed within its configured interval.
rules.why_it_matters: The monitoring source stops feeding events and nothing raises an alert about the absence of alerts. Silence is indistinguishable from healthy, which is the defining hazard of event ingestion.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_connector_instance status, last run, error records
rules.detection_logic: Connectors with error state, or last successful pull beyond interval x tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 3x interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on connector state and timestamps.
rules.evidence_to_show: Connector, source, last successful pull, error class, and the event volume trend showing where ingestion stopped.
rules.false_positive_guard: Connector deliberately paused during source maintenance.
rules.cross_domain_link: Creates a monitoring blind spot with no alert

rules.rule: Monitoring tool in the estate with no connector at all (blind spot)
rules.what_it_means: A monitoring tool is present in the estate — evidenced by CIs, integrations or credentials — with no Event Management connector configured.
rules.why_it_matters: An entire monitoring source feeds nothing into ServiceNow. Whatever it sees, ServiceNow does not. The blind spot is structural rather than a failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_connector_instance registered sources, monitoring tool CIs, integration and credential evidence
rules.detection_logic: Monitoring tools evidenced in the estate with no corresponding connector instance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tool detection from CI classes, integration endpoints and credential types
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — tool presence is inferred from indirect evidence.
rules.evidence_to_show: The tool evidenced, the evidence type, the registered connector list, and the infrastructure that tool monitors.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tool feeds ServiceNow through a different mechanism, or is deliberately not integrated.
rules.cross_domain_link: Structural monitoring blind spot

rules.rule: Connector last successful pull beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: A connector's last successful pull exceeds the threshold, without the connector being in an error state.
rules.why_it_matters: The connector reports healthy and is not producing. Distinct from ITOM-084 because nothing errors, so no operational alert fires.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_connector_instance last successful pull, status
rules.detection_logic: Connectors with status healthy but last successful pull beyond threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Threshold from the connector's own interval
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on timestamps.
rules.evidence_to_show: Connector, status, last pull, interval, and event volume trend.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source genuinely producing no events during a quiet period.
rules.cross_domain_link: Healthy-looking silent failure

rules.rule: Event ingestion volume dropped sharply (source silently stopped)
rules.what_it_means: Event ingestion volume from a source has dropped sharply, indicating the source has stopped reporting.
rules.why_it_matters: Volume-based detection catches what status-based detection misses. A source can be connected, authenticated and silent.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event volume by source across time windows
rules.detection_logic: Per source: event volume per period, flagged on a drop exceeding threshold against its own baseline
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 70% drop against a rolling baseline. Baseline must account for weekday and weekend variance.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on volume arithmetic. Baseline confidence from window length.
rules.evidence_to_show: Source, volume trend, drop onset date, connector status at that time, and the infrastructure that source monitors.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuine reduction in events after a remediation programme. Corroborate against the source's own health.
rules.cross_domain_link: Detects silent source failure that status checks miss

rules.rule: Event ingestion volume spiking beyond processing capacity
rules.what_it_means: Event ingestion volume is spiking beyond processing capacity.
rules.why_it_matters: Events are queued or discarded. The alert that matters may be in the discarded set, and nothing records which events were lost.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event volume, processing rate, queue depth, discard counts
rules.detection_logic: Ingestion rate exceeding processing rate, with queue growth or discard events
rules.threshold_parameter: Thresholds from observed processing capacity
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rate comparison and queue depth.
rules.evidence_to_show: Volume spike, processing rate, queue depth trend, discard count, and the source producing the spike.
rules.false_positive_guard: Planned load test.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes event loss with no record of what was lost

rules.rule: Connector credentials failing
rules.what_it_means: Connector credentials are failing authentication against the monitoring source.
rules.why_it_matters: The same rotation problem as discovery credentials, in a different place with the same silent failure mode.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_connector_instance error records, credential references and update timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Connectors with authentication-class errors, correlated against credential update timestamps
rules.threshold_parameter: Any sustained failure
rules.confidence_basis: 95% where the error class is explicit and correlates with a credential update.
rules.evidence_to_show: Connector, credential, error class, failure onset, and correlation with the credential's last update date.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source-side account issue rather than a credential change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Same pattern as ITOM-017 in the event domain

rules.rule: Connector instance inactive but source still live
rules.what_it_means: A connector instance is set inactive while its monitoring source remains live and producing.
rules.why_it_matters: Deliberate deactivation that nobody reversed. The source is generating events that reach nothing.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_connector_instance active flag, source liveness evidence
rules.detection_logic: Inactive connectors whose source shows evidence of continued operation
rules.threshold_parameter: Liveness evidence from source CIs, credentials or other integrations
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — source liveness is inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Connector, deactivation date and user, source liveness evidence, and the monitored infrastructure now unmonitored in ServiceNow.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source genuinely decommissioned.
rules.cross_domain_link: Withdrawn monitoring coverage

rules.rule: Event queue backlog beyond threshold
rules.what_it_means: The event processing queue depth exceeds threshold.
rules.why_it_matters: Events are arriving faster than they are being turned into alerts. Alert latency grows, and during an incident that latency is exactly when it matters most.
rules.source_tables_fields: Event queue depth and age aggregates
rules.detection_logic: Queue depth and oldest-event age against thresholds
rules.threshold_parameter: Age is the more meaningful threshold; default 15 minutes
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on queue aggregates.
rules.evidence_to_show: Queue depth and age trend, arrival versus processing rate, and the sources contributing most.
rules.false_positive_guard: Transient backlog during a known event storm.
rules.cross_domain_link: Alert latency during incidents

rules.rule: Events discarded due to processing limits
rules.what_it_means: Events are being discarded because processing limits are exceeded.
rules.why_it_matters: Data loss. Unlike a queue backlog, discarded events are gone, and there is usually no record of which ones.
rules.source_tables_fields: Event discard counts and reasons
rules.detection_logic: Discard events above threshold, grouped by reason and source
rules.threshold_parameter: Any sustained discarding
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on discard counts where recorded.
rules.evidence_to_show: Discard count by reason and source, the time windows affected, and the processing limit that triggered them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate filtering configured as a discard.
rules.cross_domain_link: Irrecoverable event loss

rules.rule: Connector with no error handling or retry configuration
rules.what_it_means: A connector has no error handling or retry configuration.
rules.why_it_matters: A single transient failure produces a permanent gap. With retry configured, the same failure self-heals.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_connector_instance error handling and retry configuration
rules.detection_logic: Connectors with no retry or error handling configured
rules.threshold_parameter: Any unconfigured connector
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Connector list, retry configuration state, and their historical transient failure count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source semantics make retry inappropriate.
rules.cross_domain_link: Turns transient failures into permanent gaps

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: No match rule exists for a CI class set receiving events
rules.what_it_means: No em_match_rule exists covering a CI class set that receives events.
rules.why_it_matters: Binding falls back to default name matching with no class filter and no precedence. Every event against that class set binds by guesswork. This is the configuration gap that made the router alert bind to the wrong record.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_match_rule catalogue, event node and class distribution
rules.detection_logic: CI class sets receiving events with no covering match rule
rules.threshold_parameter: Class coverage evaluated with hierarchy expansion
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rule coverage after hierarchy resolution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Class set, event volume against it, the absent rule coverage, and the binding outcome distribution for those events.
rules.false_positive_guard: Default binding genuinely adequate for a simple class set.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — match rule as update set
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of ITOM-096, ITOM-099 and the router demo

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Overall CI binding success rate below threshold
rules.what_it_means: The overall percentage of events that successfully bind to a CI.
rules.why_it_matters: The headline for event-to-CMDB integration. Every unbound event is an alert with no context, no impact calculation and no automatic prioritisation.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event binding outcomes, em_alert CI references
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(events binding to a CI) / COUNT(events processed) in the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 85%. Report by source and by class.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidence_to_show: Binding rate trend, by source and by class, and the dominant failure reason for unbound events.
rules.false_positive_guard: Sources producing events that legitimately have no CI (application-level business events).
rules.cross_domain_link: Determines whether Event Management can function at all

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Percentage of alerts binding to a CI with zero relationships
rules.what_it_means: The percentage of alerts that bind to a CI which has zero relationships.
rules.why_it_matters: The most important number in the entire ITOM catalogue. Binding succeeded, so every metric reports success, and impact analysis returns zero because the CI it bound to connects to nothing. This is exactly what happened on 14 March, and it is invisible to every dashboard ServiceNow ships.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert CI references, cmdb_rel_ci edge counts for those CIs
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(alerts whose bound CI has zero edges) / COUNT(alerts with a bound CI)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 15%. Escalate above 30%.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the join. The interpretation is unambiguous.
rules.evidence_to_show: The ratio, the specific CIs involved, whether each is one half of a duplicate pair, and the alerts that returned zero impact as a result.
rules.false_positive_guard: CI classes that legitimately have no relationships and are not expected to produce service impact.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for the duplicate merges, Lane 2 for the match rule
rules.cross_domain_link: The core diagnostic of the router demo; joins CMDB-033 and ITOM-094

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Match rule using name-only criteria with no class filter
rules.what_it_means: A match rule matches on name only, with no class filter and no identity attribute.
rules.why_it_matters: Guarantees ambiguous binding wherever a name appears more than once. Combined with a duplicate CI, it guarantees binding to the wrong one.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_match_rule criteria and class filters
rules.detection_logic: Match rules whose criteria contain only name-type attributes and no class restriction
rules.threshold_parameter: Attribute classification configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rule configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, its criteria, the class set it applies to, the duplicate count in that class set, and the resulting binding outcomes.
rules.false_positive_guard: Class set where name is genuinely unique and no better attribute is available.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of ITOM-099

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Events failing to bind to any CI
rules.what_it_means: Events fail to bind to any CI at all.
rules.why_it_matters: The alert exists with no context. No impact, no automatic priority, no service, no owner. Manual triage from a blank start.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event binding outcomes, node values, match rule evaluation results
rules.detection_logic: Events with no CI binding, grouped by source and by node value format
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by node format to identify the systematic cases
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on binding outcome.
rules.evidence_to_show: Unbound event count by source and node format, the match rules evaluated, and the CIs that should have matched.
rules.false_positive_guard: Events that legitimately have no CI.
rules.cross_domain_link: Direct loss of impact and prioritisation

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Events binding to the wrong CI of a duplicate pair
rules.what_it_means: Events bind to the wrong member of a duplicate CI pair — typically the one created by the monitoring integration, which has no relationships.
rules.why_it_matters: The single most damaging binding failure, because it succeeds. Every metric reports a successful bind and a completed impact calculation, and the answer is empty. Nothing in the platform indicates that the wrong record was chosen.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert CI references, duplicate set membership, edge counts per duplicate member
rules.detection_logic: Alerts bound to a duplicate set member with fewer relationships than another member of the same set
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence within a detected duplicate set
rules.confidence_basis: Inherits duplicate detection confidence, typically 92 to 97% where identity attributes match exactly.
rules.evidence_to_show: The alert, both CIs in the duplicate set, their edge counts, their creation sources, and the impact result returned versus the result the other member would have produced.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate logical-versus-physical modelling where the bound CI is the correct target.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — merge the duplicate and transfer the correlation_id
rules.cross_domain_link: The exact mechanism of the router outage

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Match rule with no precedence between multiple candidates
rules.what_it_means: A match rule has no precedence configured for resolving between multiple candidate CIs.
rules.why_it_matters: When two CIs match, the choice is arbitrary and can differ between evaluations. Binding becomes non-deterministic, so the same event can bind differently on different days.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_match_rule precedence configuration
rules.detection_logic: Match rules with multiple potential candidates and no precedence criteria
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires where the rule's class set contains duplicates
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. Impact depends on duplicate presence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, its precedence configuration, the duplicate populations in its class set, and any evidence of binding inconsistency across evaluations.
rules.false_positive_guard: Class set with no duplicates, where precedence never engages.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — precedence preferring the CI with active relationships
rules.cross_domain_link: Makes binding non-deterministic

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Binding resolving to a retired CI
rules.what_it_means: Event binding resolves to a retired or decommissioned CI.
rules.why_it_matters: The alert attaches to something that officially does not exist. Impact traverses from a retired CI, and any automatic routing goes to whoever owned a decommissioned asset.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert CI references, CI lifecycle state
rules.detection_logic: Alerts bound to CIs in a retired or decommissioned state
rules.threshold_parameter: Retired state set from instance configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on state check.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert, the retired CI, its retirement date, and the live CI the event should have bound to.
rules.false_positive_guard: CI retired in error while still live.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — correct the binding after resolving the CI state
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-080 and the binding chain

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Match rule order producing weak matches first
rules.what_it_means: Match rule order places weak criteria before strong ones, so a weak match succeeds before a strong criterion is evaluated.
rules.why_it_matters: Produces confident wrong bindings. Worse than no binding, because the alert appears correctly attributed.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_match_rule order and criteria strength
rules.detection_logic: Match rules where a descriptive-attribute rule has lower order than an identity-attribute rule for the same class set
rules.threshold_parameter: Attribute strength classification configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — strength classification is a judgement encoded in configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule order, criteria per rule, and binding outcomes showing weak-first matches.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ordering chosen deliberately for a class set where the weak criterion is reliable.
rules.cross_domain_link: Produces wrong bindings that look correct

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Node values arriving in a format no match rule handles
rules.what_it_means: Node values arrive in formats that no match rule handles: short hostname where rules expect FQDN, IP where rules expect name, case or domain-suffix variance.
rules.why_it_matters: A systematic and entirely fixable binding failure. One normalisation rule usually resolves an entire source's worth of unbound events.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event node value formats by source, match rule criteria formats
rules.detection_logic: Node value format distribution by source, compared against the formats match rules accept
rules.threshold_parameter: Format classification: FQDN, short name, IP, MAC, composite
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — format classification from pattern matching.
rules.evidence_to_show: Node format distribution by source, the formats rules accept, the unbound volume attributable to each mismatch, and the normalisation that would resolve it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Formats already normalised upstream in the connector.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — normalisation in the match rule or connector
rules.cross_domain_link: Common systematic cause of ITOM-098

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Bound CI in a class that cannot participate in impact calculation
rules.what_it_means: Events bind to a CI in a class that cannot participate in impact calculation.
rules.why_it_matters: Binding succeeds and impact still returns nothing, because the class sits outside the service model. A second, subtler version of the ITOM-096 failure.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert CI references and classes, impact calculation class participation
rules.detection_logic: Alerts bound to CIs in classes that do not participate in service impact
rules.threshold_parameter: Participating class set from the impact configuration
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on class participation configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert, bound CI class, the impact-participating class set, and the CI that should have been bound.
rules.false_positive_guard: Classes deliberately excluded from impact.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 or Lane 3 depending on whether the class or the binding is wrong
rules.cross_domain_link: Second-order cause of zero-impact alerts

rules.group: 4B. CI binding — the router demo core
rules.rule: Match rule defined but disabled
rules.what_it_means: A match rule is defined but disabled.
rules.why_it_matters: Configuration present, effect absent. Someone disabled it to troubleshoot and did not re-enable it, and the class set it covered reverted to default binding.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_match_rule active flag, class coverage
rules.detection_logic: Match rules with active=false whose class set receives events
rules.threshold_parameter: Any disabled rule with live event volume in its class set
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rule state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, disable date and user, its class set, event volume in that set, and the binding outcomes since it was disabled.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rule superseded by a newer rule covering the same classes.
rules.cross_domain_link: Reverts the class set to ITOM-094 conditions

rules.rule: Impact calculation returning zero affected services on Critical alerts
rules.what_it_means: Critical alerts are returning zero affected services from impact calculation.
rules.why_it_matters: The calculation ran and produced nothing. Distinct from a failure, because nothing errors — the graph was traversed and it was empty. This is the number that turns an abstract CMDB score into an operational argument, and it is the headline metric of the router demo.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert impact results, bound CI relationship depth, service association
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(Critical alerts with empty affected-service result) / COUNT(Critical alerts with a bound CI)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 20%. Escalate above 40%.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the impact result. The cause attribution per alert is computed from the bound CI's edge state.
rules.evidence_to_show: The ratio, the alerts, their bound CIs, the edge count on each, and a per-alert cause: zero edges, duplicate binding, or no path to a service.
rules.false_positive_guard: Alerts on CI classes outside the service model by design.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 for the CI-level causes, Lane 3 for the CSDM structural causes
rules.cross_domain_link: The operational consequence of CMDB-057, CMDB-033 and ITOM-094 combined

rules.rule: Business service impact never populated on any alert
rules.what_it_means: Business service impact is never populated on any alert across the entire estate.
rules.why_it_matters: Impact calculation is either not configured or structurally unable to produce a result. The Event Management investment delivers alerting without context, which is most of the cost and little of the value.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert business service fields across the full alert population
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(alerts with business service populated) = 0 across the window
rules.threshold_parameter: Fires only on a full-population zero
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — a complete absence is not an inference.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert volume, zero business-service population, the impact configuration state, and the CSDM reachability figure explaining it.
rules.false_positive_guard: Estate deliberately does not use service-based impact.
rules.cross_domain_link: Structural failure of the Event Management value proposition

rules.rule: Alert with no assignment and no notification path
rules.what_it_means: Alerts exist with no assignment group and no notification path.
rules.why_it_matters: The alert fires into an empty room. Nobody is told and nobody owns it. It sits in the console until someone happens to look.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert assignment, notification rule coverage
rules.detection_logic: Alerts with no assignment group AND no matching notification rule
rules.threshold_parameter: Both absent
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on assignment and rule coverage.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert count by severity and source, their age, and the absent assignment and notification configuration.
rules.false_positive_guard: Informational-severity alerts that are deliberately unassigned.
rules.cross_domain_link: Alerts that reach nobody

rules.rule: Alerts ageing beyond threshold with no acknowledgement
rules.what_it_means: Alerts are ageing beyond threshold with no acknowledgement.
rules.why_it_matters: Either they do not matter, in which case they are noise, or they do, in which case nobody is responding. Both readings are actionable and the distinction is made by severity distribution.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert state, age, acknowledgement timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Open unacknowledged alerts beyond age threshold, by severity
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold by severity; default 4 hours Critical, 24 hours Major
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on age arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert count and age distribution by severity and source, with the assignment group for each.
rules.false_positive_guard: Alerts in a known suppression window.
rules.cross_domain_link: Distinguishes noise from unstaffed response

rules.rule: Severity distribution skewed so nearly everything is Critical
rules.what_it_means: The alert severity distribution is skewed so that nearly everything is Critical.
rules.why_it_matters: When everything is critical, nothing is. Severity stops carrying information and triage reverts to whoever shouts loudest. Almost always a rule-configuration artefact rather than a genuine estate condition.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert severity distribution by source and rule
rules.detection_logic: Severity distribution where one band exceeds threshold share
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 60% in a single band. Report by source, since one source usually causes it.
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on distribution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Severity distribution overall and by source, the rules assigning severity, and the correlation between Critical alerts and actual incident creation.
rules.false_positive_guard: An estate genuinely in crisis during the observation window.
rules.cross_domain_link: Destroys the information value of severity

rules.rule: Alerts with no matching alert rule, so no action ever fires
rules.what_it_means: Alerts exist for which no alert rule matches, so no action is ever taken on them.
rules.why_it_matters: The alert is created and nothing downstream happens: no incident, no notification, no task. It is a log entry with a severity field.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert records, em alert rule evaluation results
rules.detection_logic: Alerts with no matching alert rule, grouped by source and type
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by alert type to find the systematic gaps
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rule matching results.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert count by type and source with no matching rule, and the rule catalogue for comparison.
rules.false_positive_guard: Alert types deliberately left unactioned.
rules.cross_domain_link: Alerts that produce no action

rules.rule: Alert rules firing but with no configured action
rules.what_it_means: Alert rules match and fire but have no configured action.
rules.why_it_matters: Subtler than ITOM-111 because the rule exists and evaluates. It simply does nothing when it matches, which reads as configured on every screen.
rules.source_tables_fields: Alert rule definitions and action configuration, firing counts
rules.detection_logic: Alert rules with firing events but no configured action
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence with non-zero firing count
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rule configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule, firing count, absent action configuration, and the alerts affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Rule used purely for correlation or grouping, where no action is intended.
rules.cross_domain_link: Configured-but-inert rules

rules.rule: Deduplication not occurring — alert count tracking event count one to one
rules.what_it_means: Deduplication is not occurring — alert count tracks event count approximately one to one.
rules.why_it_matters: The console fills with duplicates of the same condition. Operators triage the same problem repeatedly and real alerts are buried. Usually a missing dedup key rather than a broken engine.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event and em_alert counts, alert dedup counts
rules.detection_logic: Alert count / event count ratio approaching 1, with alert dedup counts near zero
rules.threshold_parameter: Ratio threshold default 0.8
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio arithmetic.
rules.evidence_to_show: Event and alert volume, the ratio, dedup count distribution, and the sources with the worst ratio.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuinely distinct events with no valid dedup key.
rules.cross_domain_link: Console noise; buries real alerts

rules.rule: Alert correlation rules absent for known parent-child device patterns
rules.what_it_means: No alert correlation rules exist for parent-child device patterns that are present in the estate.
rules.why_it_matters: A switch failure generates an alert for the switch and every device behind it. Without correlation, the operator sees forty alerts and must work out which one is the cause. Correlation is what turns forty into one.
rules.source_tables_fields: em correlation rule catalogue, CI relationship patterns, historical alert co-occurrence
rules.detection_logic: Parent-child CI patterns with recurring alert co-occurrence and no covering correlation rule
rules.threshold_parameter: Co-occurrence threshold configurable; requires relationship data to identify the pattern
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — pattern identification from co-occurrence is statistical.
rules.evidence_to_show: The co-occurring alert pattern, the underlying CI relationship, historical frequency, and the absent correlation rule.
rules.false_positive_guard: Patterns already correlated by a different mechanism.
rules.cross_domain_link: Depends on relationship completeness to be detectable at all

rules.rule: Event flood from a single source or node
rules.what_it_means: A single source or node is flooding the system with events.
rules.why_it_matters: Consumes processing capacity, fills queues, and can push out events that matter. One misbehaving device can degrade monitoring for the entire estate.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_event volume by source and by node
rules.detection_logic: Sources or nodes whose event volume exceeds threshold share of total
rules.threshold_parameter: Default 20% of total volume from a single node
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on volume distribution.
rules.evidence_to_show: Volume by source and node, the flooding node, its event types, and the queue impact during flood periods.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimately high-volume source such as a large monitoring platform.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 2 — fix the source, then add a rate limit
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM-088, ITOM-091, ITOM-092

rules.rule: Alert-to-incident creation not configured for Critical severities
rules.what_it_means: Alert-to-incident creation is not configured for Critical severity alerts.
rules.why_it_matters: Critical alerts never become tickets. The response depends entirely on somebody watching the console, which at three in the morning is a fragile assumption.
rules.source_tables_fields: Alert rule incident-creation configuration by severity
rules.detection_logic: Critical severity alerts with no incident-creation rule covering them
rules.threshold_parameter: Severity bands configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on rule coverage.
rules.evidence_to_show: Critical alert volume, incident creation rate against it, and the rule coverage gap.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate manual triage model with staffed console coverage.
rules.cross_domain_link: Response depends on human console watching

rules.rule: Alert closure not tied to event resolution (manual close backlog)
rules.what_it_means: Alert closure is not tied to event resolution, producing a manual close backlog.
rules.why_it_matters: Alerts stay open after the condition clears. The console shows problems that no longer exist, and operators learn to ignore it.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert state, resolution event correlation, close timestamps
rules.detection_logic: Alerts remaining open after a corresponding resolution event was received
rules.threshold_parameter: Correlation by dedup key and node
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — resolution event correlation depends on the source sending clear events.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert count open after resolution, the resolution events received, and the age distribution.
rules.false_positive_guard: Source does not send clear events, so automatic closure is impossible. Report as a source capability gap.
rules.cross_domain_link: Console credibility

rules.rule: Alert rule conditions never reviewed since creation
rules.what_it_means: Alert rule conditions have not been reviewed since creation despite significant age.
rules.why_it_matters: Rules written for an estate that has since changed. They fire on conditions that no longer mean what they meant, and nobody has checked.
rules.source_tables_fields: Alert rule creation and update history, firing volume
rules.detection_logic: Rules with no update since creation, above age threshold, with non-zero firing volume
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 365 days
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on update history.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rule list with creation date, last update, firing volume, and the incident conversion rate for alerts they produce.
rules.false_positive_guard: Stable rules that genuinely need no revision.
rules.cross_domain_link: Rule relevance decay

rules.rule: Alerts never actioned and auto-closed by age
rules.what_it_means: Alerts are never actioned and are auto-closed by age.
rules.why_it_matters: Volume-based evidence that these alerts carry no value. Either the rule producing them should be retired or the condition genuinely does not need a response.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert closure method, action history
rules.detection_logic: Alerts closed by age with zero acknowledgement or action, grouped by rule and source
rules.threshold_parameter: Report by rule to identify the systematic cases
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on closure method and action history.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert count auto-closed by rule and source, with the proportion of total volume each represents.
rules.false_positive_guard: Alerts deliberately informational with no expected action.
rules.cross_domain_link: Identifies rules producing pure noise

rules.rule: Cloud account present in the organisation with no service account registered
rules.what_it_means: A cloud account or subscription exists in the organisation with no service account registered in ServiceNow.
rules.why_it_matters: An entire cloud estate is invisible. Resources are being created and paid for with no CMDB representation, no service association and no governance.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud service account registrations, evidence of cloud accounts from tags, CIs, integrations or billing references
rules.detection_logic: Cloud accounts evidenced in the estate with no registered service account
rules.threshold_parameter: Account evidence from cloud CI account identifiers and integration references
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — account existence is inferred from indirect evidence.
rules.evidence_to_show: The account evidenced, the evidence type, registered account list, and the resources attributable to the unregistered account.
rules.false_positive_guard: Account managed through a different tooling chain by design.
rules.cross_domain_link: Structural cloud blind spot; precursor to shadow estate

rules.rule: Cloud discovery coverage below threshold vs. known subscriptions or accounts
rules.what_it_means: Cloud discovery coverage is below threshold relative to known subscriptions, accounts, regions and resource types.
rules.why_it_matters: Partial cloud visibility presented as complete. The CMDB shows cloud resources, so the team believes cloud is covered, while whole regions or resource types are absent.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud discovery schedules and scope, registered accounts, discovered resource counts by account and region
rules.detection_logic: COUNT(accounts and regions with current discovery) / COUNT(registered accounts and regions)
rules.threshold_parameter: Default threshold 90%
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the ratio against registered scope. Coverage against actual cloud estate depends on ITOM-120.
rules.evidence_to_show: Coverage by account, region and resource type, with the gaps ranked by estimated resource count.
rules.false_positive_guard: Regions deliberately excluded.
rules.cross_domain_link: Partial visibility presented as complete

rules.rule: Cloud CIs and on-prem CIs modelled in inconsistent classes
rules.what_it_means: Cloud resources and equivalent on-premises resources are modelled in inconsistent CI classes.
rules.why_it_matters: The same logical thing has two representations depending on where it runs. Every rule, report and service model must handle both, and most handle only one.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud CI classes, on-premises equivalent classes, class attribute profiles
rules.detection_logic: Cloud and on-premises class pairs representing equivalent resource types with divergent class assignment
rules.threshold_parameter: Equivalence mapping configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — equivalence is a modelling judgement.
rules.evidence_to_show: The class pairs, their attribute profiles, row counts, and the rules and services that cover one but not the other.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate modelling distinction with documented rationale.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes rules and service models to cover half the estate

rules.rule: Cloud service account credentials failing or expired
rules.what_it_means: Cloud service account credentials are failing or expired.
rules.why_it_matters: Cloud discovery stops. Cloud resources go stale immediately, and cloud estates change far faster than on-premises, so staleness becomes material within days rather than months.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud service account credential state, cloud discovery run errors
rules.detection_logic: Cloud accounts with authentication-class discovery failures or expired credentials
rules.threshold_parameter: Any sustained failure
rules.confidence_basis: 95% where the error class is explicit.
rules.evidence_to_show: Account, credential state and expiry, failure onset, and the resource count now going stale.
rules.false_positive_guard: Credential rotation in progress with a replacement staged.
rules.cross_domain_link: Rapid cloud CI staleness

rules.rule: Cloud discovery schedule inactive or failing
rules.what_it_means: A cloud discovery schedule is inactive or failing.
rules.why_it_matters: Same effect as ITOM-123 from a different cause. Cloud CI accuracy degrades quickly because the underlying estate is ephemeral.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud discovery schedule state and run history
rules.detection_logic: Cloud schedules inactive, or with no successful run within interval x tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Tolerance default 2x interval; cloud intervals are typically short
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on schedule state and run history.
rules.evidence_to_show: Schedule, state, last successful run, the account and regions covered, and resource staleness since.
rules.false_positive_guard: Schedule paused during an account migration.
rules.cross_domain_link: Cloud CI staleness

rules.rule: Cloud resources discovered but not linked to any application service
rules.what_it_means: Cloud resources are discovered into the CMDB but are not linked to any application service.
rules.why_it_matters: Cloud infrastructure exists in the CMDB and is outside the service model. Cloud events and changes never reach a service, which is the cloud version of the router problem.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud CIs, svc_ci_assoc, cmdb_rel_ci service edges
rules.detection_logic: Cloud-class CIs with no association or relationship path to an application service
rules.threshold_parameter: Scope to cloud classes expected to participate in the service model
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on association absence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Cloud CI count by class and account, their tags, and the services those tags suggest.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cloud resources legitimately outside the service model.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where tags indicate the service, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Cloud version of CMDB-115 and ITOM-077

rules.rule: Cloud API rate limiting causing incomplete collection
rules.what_it_means: Cloud provider API rate limiting is causing incomplete collection.
rules.why_it_matters: Discovery completes and silently returns a partial resource set. No error, no indication of what was missed, and the missing resources look identical to resources that do not exist.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud discovery run logs for rate-limit responses, resource counts across runs
rules.detection_logic: Cloud discovery runs with rate-limit error responses, or resource count variance across consecutive runs
rules.threshold_parameter: Variance threshold configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — rate limiting is identified from error responses where the provider returns them explicitly.
rules.evidence_to_show: Rate limit error count by account and API, resource count variance across runs, and the regions affected.
rules.false_positive_guard: Genuine resource count fluctuation in an elastic environment. Compare against known scaling events.
rules.cross_domain_link: Silent partial collection

rules.rule: Regions or subscriptions excluded from the schedule without justification
rules.what_it_means: Regions or subscriptions are excluded from the cloud discovery schedule with no documented justification.
rules.why_it_matters: Deliberate-looking scope reduction that may be accidental. Excluded regions hold real resources that appear nowhere.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud discovery schedule scope, registered account region list
rules.detection_logic: Registered regions or subscriptions absent from active discovery scope
rules.threshold_parameter: Any exclusion without a registered justification
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on scope comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Excluded regions and subscriptions, the resources indicated in them from billing or tag evidence, and the exclusion configuration.
rules.false_positive_guard: Regions genuinely unused.
rules.cross_domain_link: Undocumented cloud blind spot

rules.rule: Cloud service account with excessive IAM permissions
rules.what_it_means: The cloud service account holds IAM permissions beyond what discovery requires.
rules.why_it_matters: A read-only discovery role is sufficient for almost all collection. Excess permissions on a credential held in ServiceNow and used by a MID is a meaningful cloud security exposure.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud service account IAM policy where retrievable, required permission set for discovery
rules.detection_logic: Service accounts holding write, delete or admin permissions where discovery requires read only
rules.threshold_parameter: Required permission set per provider and discovery scope
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on IAM policy visibility through the API.
rules.evidence_to_show: Account, its permission set, the required read-only set, and the excess permissions with what each grants.
rules.false_positive_guard: Account shared with a provisioning function that legitimately requires write access. Recommend separation.
rules.cross_domain_link: Cloud security exposure; routes to the security reviewer

rules.rule: Cloud CIs going stale — resource terminated in cloud, still Operational in CMDB
rules.what_it_means: Cloud resources terminated at the provider remain Operational in the CMDB.
rules.why_it_matters: The CMDB asserts infrastructure that no longer exists. Impact analysis includes terminated resources, and cost and capacity reporting is overstated.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud CI lifecycle state, last successful cloud discovery, provider resource presence
rules.detection_logic: Cloud CIs marked Operational that were absent from the most recent successful discovery of their account
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires a successful recent discovery run; absence during a failed run is not evidence of termination
rules.confidence_basis: 95% where the discovery run succeeded. Drops to unusable if the run failed — guard on run success.
rules.evidence_to_show: CI, last seen in discovery, run success status, account, and any cost data showing the resource stopped billing.
rules.false_positive_guard: Resource stopped rather than terminated. Check the provider state field rather than presence alone.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — retire the CI, reversible, guarded on run success
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds ITOM-155 and CMDB-080

rules.rule: Tag-based classification failing or tags missing on cloud resources
rules.what_it_means: Tag-based classification is failing, or required tags are absent on cloud resources.
rules.why_it_matters: Tags are the only practical way to associate cloud resources with services, owners and cost centres. Without them the cloud estate is a list of resources with no business meaning.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud CI tag data, tag-based classification rule results, required tag policy
rules.detection_logic: Cloud resources missing required tags, or whose tags fail to match any classification rule
rules.threshold_parameter: Required tag set from the customer's policy; report the absence of a policy separately
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on tag presence where a policy exists.
rules.evidence_to_show: Untagged or mis-tagged resource count by account and type, the required tag set, and the classification rules that failed to match.
rules.false_positive_guard: Resource types the provider does not support tagging on.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 2 — tag remediation at source, then enforcement at provisioning
rules.cross_domain_link: Blocks cloud service association and cost allocation

rules.rule: Cloud resource cost attributes not collected
rules.what_it_means: Cloud resource cost attributes are not being collected.
rules.why_it_matters: Blocks showback, chargeback and any cost-aware optimisation. Operationally harmless, commercially significant, and often the reason a cloud programme cannot demonstrate value.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud CI cost attributes, cloud discovery configuration for billing data
rules.detection_logic: Cloud CIs with no cost attributes where cost collection is available for that provider and resource type
rules.threshold_parameter: Availability per provider and resource type
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on attribute presence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Resource count without cost data by account and type, and the cost collection configuration state.
rules.false_positive_guard: Cost managed entirely in a provider-native or third-party tool.
rules.cross_domain_link: Blocks cloud financial management

rules.rule: Multi-cloud accounts with inconsistent discovery intervals
rules.what_it_means: Multi-cloud accounts are configured with inconsistent discovery intervals.
rules.why_it_matters: One provider's resources are current and another's are days old. Any cross-cloud view mixes two different points in time without indicating it.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud discovery schedule intervals by provider and account
rules.detection_logic: Interval variance across accounts beyond threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Variance threshold configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on interval comparison.
rules.evidence_to_show: Interval by account and provider, resource counts, and the resulting staleness differential.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate variance reflecting genuinely different rates of change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Cross-cloud views mix time points

rules.rule: Cloud discovery duplicating CIs already found by agent-based discovery
rules.what_it_means: Cloud discovery creates CIs for resources already discovered by agent-based or network discovery.
rules.why_it_matters: Two sources, two records, one machine. The cloud version of the asymmetric duplicate, and it carries the same hazard: events bind to one and relationships live on the other.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud CI and agent-discovered CI identity attributes, duplicate set membership by source pair
rules.detection_logic: Duplicate sets whose members were created by cloud discovery and by agent or network discovery respectively
rules.threshold_parameter: Match on instance ID, private IP, MAC or hostname
rules.confidence_basis: Inherits duplicate detection confidence; typically 92% on instance ID or private IP match.
rules.evidence_to_show: Both CIs, their sources, identity attributes, edge counts, and the identification rule that should have merged them.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate separation of the cloud resource object from the guest OS CI.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — merge with correlation_id transfer, or Lane 2 for the identification rule
rules.cross_domain_link: Cloud instance of CMDB-033 and CMDB-039

rules.rule: Provisioning path exists that bypasses CMDB registration entirely
rules.what_it_means: A provisioning path exists that creates cloud resources without registering them in the CMDB.
rules.why_it_matters: Resources are created through an approved mechanism and are invisible. Unlike shadow IT, this is sanctioned provisioning with a governance gap, which makes it both more common and harder to argue against.
rules.source_tables_fields: Provisioning workflow definitions, CMDB registration steps, resource creation attribution
rules.detection_logic: Provisioning paths whose workflow contains no CMDB registration step, or whose outputs have no corresponding CI
rules.threshold_parameter: Any path without registration
rules.confidence_basis: 95% — path analysis depends on workflow introspection completeness.
rules.evidence_to_show: The provisioning path, its workflow, the absent registration step, and the resources created through it with no CI.
rules.false_positive_guard: Path relies on subsequent discovery for registration. Verify discovery actually covers the target account.
rules.cross_domain_link: Structural cause of shadow estate growth

rules.rule: Resources provisioned outside ServiceNow with no reconciliation back (shadow estate)
rules.what_it_means: Resources are provisioned outside ServiceNow entirely, with no reconciliation feeding them back.
rules.why_it_matters: The shadow estate. Resources exist, are billed, and appear in no governance process. Usually discovered only through the cloud bill.
rules.source_tables_fields: Cloud discovery resource counts versus ServiceNow-provisioned resource counts, provisioning request records
rules.detection_logic: Cloud resources present in discovery with no corresponding provisioning request or approval record
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires cloud discovery to be working; guard on ITOM-121 coverage
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on provisioning request attribution being traceable.
rules.evidence_to_show: Resource count with no provisioning lineage by account, their creation dates and creators, tags, and estimated cost.
rules.false_positive_guard: Resources provisioned before ServiceNow provisioning was introduced.
rules.cross_domain_link: Shadow estate quantification; the finding that reaches the CFO

rules.rule: No policy enforcement on provisioning requests
rules.what_it_means: No policy enforcement exists on provisioning requests — no quota check, no tagging requirement, no approval gate, no naming standard.
rules.why_it_matters: Provisioning is a request form with no controls. Every downstream governance problem (untagged, unowned, over-quota, orphaned) originates here, which makes this the Systemic finding of the provisioning group.
rules.source_tables_fields: Provisioning workflow policy steps, quota, tagging and approval configuration
rules.detection_logic: Provisioning paths with no policy enforcement steps configured
rules.threshold_parameter: Any path with zero enforcement
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration presence.
rules.evidence_to_show: Provisioning paths, their workflow steps, the absent policy controls, and the downstream defect counts attributable to each missing control.
rules.false_positive_guard: Policy enforced at the cloud provider level rather than in ServiceNow.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of ITOM-137, 141, 143, 145

rules.rule: Provisioned resources with no owner or cost centre
rules.what_it_means: Provisioned resources have no owner or cost centre populated.
rules.why_it_matters: Nobody is accountable for the resource and nobody is charged for it. Both are the reason unused cloud resources survive for years.
rules.source_tables_fields: Provisioned resource CIs, ownership and cost centre fields, provisioning request records
rules.detection_logic: Provisioned resources with empty owner AND empty cost centre
rules.threshold_parameter: Both absent
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Resource count by account, their cost, the requesting user from the provisioning record, and the absent ownership.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership held at the account or subscription level by design.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 where the provisioning requester is recoverable, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.cross_domain_link: Feeds CMDB-105 and blocks cost allocation

rules.rule: Provisioning failures with orphaned partial resources left running
rules.what_it_means: Provisioning failures leave orphaned partial resources running at the provider.
rules.why_it_matters: The request failed, the user retried, and the partial resources from the first attempt are still billing. Invisible in ServiceNow because the request shows as failed.
rules.source_tables_fields: Failed provisioning requests, cloud discovery resources with no successful provisioning lineage, creation timestamp correlation
rules.detection_logic: Cloud resources whose creation time correlates with a failed provisioning request and which have no successful lineage
rules.threshold_parameter: Correlation window configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 85% — correlation by timestamp and requester is circumstantial.
rules.evidence_to_show: Failed request, the resources created in its window, their current state and cost, and the absence of a rollback record.
rules.false_positive_guard: Resources legitimately created by a different concurrent request.
rules.cross_domain_link: Ongoing cost with no owner or record

rules.rule: Blueprints or templates referencing deprecated images or sizes
rules.what_it_means: Provisioning blueprints or templates reference deprecated images, instance sizes or service versions.
rules.why_it_matters: New resources are provisioned onto deprecated foundations. The technical debt is created at the moment of provisioning, which makes it entirely preventable.
rules.source_tables_fields: Blueprint and template definitions, provider deprecation data where available
rules.detection_logic: Blueprints referencing images, sizes or versions flagged deprecated by the provider
rules.threshold_parameter: Deprecation data per provider
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on deprecation data availability.
rules.evidence_to_show: Blueprint, the deprecated reference, the provider deprecation date, the resources already provisioned from it, and the recommended replacement.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deprecated reference retained deliberately for compatibility.
rules.cross_domain_link: Creates technical debt at provisioning time

rules.rule: Decommission workflow not retiring the corresponding CI
rules.what_it_means: The decommission workflow terminates the cloud resource but does not retire the corresponding CI.
rules.why_it_matters: Produces ITOM-129 systematically rather than incidentally. The CMDB accumulates operational records for resources that were deliberately destroyed through an approved process.
rules.source_tables_fields: Decommission workflow definitions, CI retirement steps, terminated resource CI states
rules.detection_logic: Decommission workflows with no CI retirement step, or terminated resources whose CIs remain Operational
rules.threshold_parameter: Any workflow without the step
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on workflow configuration. Resource correlation at 95%.
rules.evidence_to_show: Decommission workflow, the absent retirement step, and the count of terminated resources with Operational CIs.
rules.false_positive_guard: CI retirement handled by a separate scheduled reconciliation. Verify it runs.
rules.cross_domain_link: Systematic cause of ITOM-129 and ITOM-155

rules.rule: Quota or budget policy defined but not enforced
rules.what_it_means: Quota or budget policies are defined but not enforced at provisioning time.
rules.why_it_matters: The policy exists and is advisory. Overspend is detected after the fact by the bill rather than prevented at the request, which is the difference between governance and reporting.
rules.source_tables_fields: Quota and budget policy definitions, provisioning workflow enforcement steps, actual consumption against quota
rules.detection_logic: Defined quotas with no enforcement step in the provisioning path, or actual consumption exceeding quota with no blocked requests
rules.threshold_parameter: Any defined-but-unenforced policy
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on enforcement configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Policy, defined limit, actual consumption, the absent enforcement step, and the requests that exceeded it without being blocked.
rules.false_positive_guard: Enforcement handled at the provider level.
rules.cross_domain_link: Governance that reports rather than controls

rules.rule: Provisioning approvals routed to inactive users or empty groups
rules.what_it_means: Provisioning approvals are routed to inactive users or groups with no active members.
rules.why_it_matters: Requests hang indefinitely. Users learn to route around ServiceNow provisioning, which then produces ITOM-135 shadow estate. The two findings are causally linked.
rules.source_tables_fields: Provisioning approval configuration, sys_user.active, sys_user_grmember
rules.detection_logic: Approval routing resolving to inactive users or groups with zero active members
rules.threshold_parameter: Active membership resolved live
rules.confidence_basis: 100% — the approver resolves to someone active or does not.
rules.evidence_to_show: Approval configuration, the resolved approver state, the hanging requests and their ages, and the shadow provisioning that followed.
rules.false_positive_guard: Approver deactivated within a grace period with a delegate configured.
rules.cross_domain_link: Causes ITOM-135; cross-links to Data Quality Q2

rules.rule: Untagged resources not blocked at provisioning time
rules.what_it_means: Untagged resources are not blocked at provisioning time.
rules.why_it_matters: Tagging enforced after the fact never succeeds, because nobody goes back. The only effective point of enforcement is provisioning, and it is not enforced there.
rules.source_tables_fields: Provisioning workflow tag enforcement, tag policy, resulting untagged resource counts
rules.detection_logic: Provisioning paths with no tag enforcement step, joined to untagged resource counts from those paths
rules.threshold_parameter: Required tag set from policy
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on enforcement configuration.
rules.evidence_to_show: Provisioning path, absent enforcement, the required tags, and the untagged resource count and cost originating from that path.
rules.false_positive_guard: Tagging applied post-provisioning by an automated process. Verify it works.
rules.cross_domain_link: Root cause of ITOM-130

rules.rule: Blueprint drift — deployed configuration differing from the template
rules.what_it_means: Deployed resource configuration has drifted from the blueprint or template it was provisioned from.
rules.why_it_matters: The blueprint no longer describes what is running. Security and compliance assumptions based on the blueprint are invalid, and nobody knows which resources have drifted.
rules.source_tables_fields: Blueprint definitions, deployed resource attributes from cloud discovery
rules.detection_logic: Deployed resources whose attributes differ from their source blueprint beyond tolerance
rules.threshold_parameter: Attribute comparison set and tolerance configurable
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — depends on blueprint-to-resource lineage being traceable.
rules.evidence_to_show: Resource, its blueprint, the differing attributes with both values, and the change history if available.
rules.false_positive_guard: Deliberate post-provisioning modification through an approved change.
rules.cross_domain_link: Invalidates blueprint-based compliance assumptions

rules.rule: No lease or expiry on non-production provisioned resources
rules.what_it_means: Non-production provisioned resources have no lease or expiry configured.
rules.why_it_matters: Test and development resources run indefinitely. In most estates this is the largest single component of avoidable cloud spend.
rules.source_tables_fields: Provisioned resource lease and expiry configuration, environment tags, resource age
rules.detection_logic: Non-production resources with no lease or expiry, above age threshold
rules.threshold_parameter: Age threshold default 90 days; environment from tags or used_for
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on configuration. Environment classification depends on tagging quality.
rules.evidence_to_show: Resource count and cost by account, their age, environment classification, and last activity indicators.
rules.false_positive_guard: Long-lived non-production environments that are deliberately permanent.
rules.cross_domain_link: Largest avoidable cloud cost component in most estates

rules.rule: Provisioning catalogue items with no owner
rules.what_it_means: Provisioning catalogue items have no owner.
rules.why_it_matters: When the item breaks or needs updating, nobody knows who owns it. Low consequence until the day it matters.
rules.source_tables_fields: sc_cat_item owner field for provisioning items
rules.detection_logic: Provisioning catalogue items with empty owner
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on field state.
rules.evidence_to_show: Item list, creation date, order volume, and absent owner.
rules.false_positive_guard: Ownership held at the catalogue category level.
rules.cross_domain_link: Governance hygiene

rules.rule: Credential failure on a range directly causing CI staleness, with the affected CI count attached
rules.what_it_means: A credential failure on a specific range is the traced cause of CI staleness, with the affected CI count computed and attached to the finding.
rules.why_it_matters: This is the join that no dashboard produces. ITOM reports a credential failure. CMDB reports stale CIs. Nobody computes the arrow between them, so the credential failure is triaged as a discovery nuisance rather than as the cause of estate-wide CMDB decay.
rules.source_tables_fields: discovery_device_history failures by credential and range, cmdb_ci.last_discovered for CIs in that range, temporal correlation
rules.detection_logic: For each failing credential: COUNT(CIs in its ranges whose last_discovered postdates the failure onset) attributed as caused
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires failure onset date and per-CI staleness; attribute only CIs whose staleness began after onset
rules.confidence_basis: Computed from temporal alignment: CIs whose staleness onset falls within the failure window, divided by CIs in range. State the alignment method.
rules.evidence_to_show: The credential, failure onset, the range, the CI staleness curve before and after onset, and the attributed CI count with the control group for contrast.
rules.false_positive_guard: CIs stale for an unrelated prior reason. Attribute only the delta after failure onset, never the total stale population.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — credential correction, then targeted rediscovery
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins ITOM-017 to CMDB-072; the first link in the router chain

rules.rule: Discovery failure causing relationship collapse, quantified
rules.what_it_means: A discovery failure is the traced cause of relationship collapse, with the lost edge count quantified.
rules.why_it_matters: The second link in the chain. When discovery stops confirming a device, the reconciliation process removes the relationships it previously maintained. The edges disappear silently and the graph degrades without any deletion event that a human would notice.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_rel_ci counts across snapshots, sys_audit relationship deletions, discovery failure windows
rules.detection_logic: Relationship deletions whose timestamps fall within a discovery failure window for the affected CIs, counted and attributed
rules.threshold_parameter: Deletion attribution requires audit retention covering the window
rules.confidence_basis: Computed from temporal alignment of deletion events to failure onset. State audit retention coverage.
rules.evidence_to_show: Failure window, relationship count before and after, the deletion events with their deleting process, and the affected CIs and services.
rules.false_positive_guard: Relationships deleted by a deliberate decommissioning in the same window. Cross-check change records.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — restore from an independent topology source once discovery is fixed
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins ITOM-017 to CMDB-056; the second link in the router chain

rules.rule: Weak identification rule plus a monitoring integration jointly producing duplicates
rules.what_it_means: A weak identification rule combined with a monitoring integration is jointly producing duplicate CIs, where neither component alone would.
rules.why_it_matters: Neither the identification rule nor the integration is wrong in isolation. Together they produce a duplicate for every monitored device. This is why single-domain analysis never finds the cause: it is in the interaction.
rules.source_tables_fields: cmdb_identifier criteria, integration CI creation attribution, duplicate set membership by source pair
rules.detection_logic: Duplicate sets where one member originates from a monitoring integration and the identification rule's criteria do not include the attributes that integration populates
rules.threshold_parameter: Requires both the rule criteria and the integration's attribute payload
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — attribution of the joint cause is inferential but strongly evidenced by the attribute overlap analysis.
rules.evidence_to_show: The identification rule and its criteria, the integration and the attributes it writes, the non-overlap between them, and the duplicate count produced.
rules.false_positive_guard: Duplicates caused by one component alone. Test by checking whether duplicates exist from other sources under the same rule.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 2 — amend the identification rule or the integration payload
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins CMDB-044 to the monitoring integration; the third link in the router chain

rules.rule: Alert binding to the duplicate CI that carries no relationships
rules.what_it_means: Alerts are binding to the duplicate CI that carries no relationships, quantified across the alert population.
rules.why_it_matters: The fourth and decisive link. Everything upstream produced a duplicate; this is where it becomes an outage. The bind succeeds, the impact calculation runs, and the answer is empty. No metric anywhere in the platform reports a problem.
rules.source_tables_fields: em_alert CI references, duplicate set membership, edge counts per member, impact results
rules.detection_logic: Alerts bound to a duplicate set member with zero edges where another member of the set has edges, with the impact result for each
rules.threshold_parameter: Any occurrence; report as a count and as a share of total alerts
rules.confidence_basis: Inherits duplicate detection confidence. The impact consequence is observed, not inferred.
rules.evidence_to_show: Alert, both CIs with edge counts and sources, the impact result returned, and the impact result the other member would have returned.
rules.false_positive_guard: Legitimate logical-versus-physical modelling where the bound CI is correct.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 1 — merge and transfer correlation_id, then Lane 2 for the match rule
rules.cross_domain_link: The final link; this is the 14 March failure in one finding

rules.rule: Service map incomplete because the underlying discovery failed on that tier
rules.what_it_means: A service map is incomplete because discovery failed on a specific tier, with the tier and the cause identified.
rules.why_it_matters: Explains map incompleteness rather than merely reporting it. Without the join, the map looks like a mapping problem and the team tunes mapping configuration that was never wrong.
rules.source_tables_fields: Map topology by tier, discovery success rates by tier and range, credential and pattern failures
rules.detection_logic: Map tiers with missing CIs, correlated against discovery failure for the CI classes in that tier
rules.threshold_parameter: Tier classification from CI class
rules.confidence_basis: 90% — correlation between map gap and discovery failure on the same class and range.
rules.evidence_to_show: Map, the missing tier, the discovery failure evidence for that tier's classes, and the map CI count before and after the failure onset.
rules.false_positive_guard: Map scoped deliberately to exclude that tier.
rules.cross_domain_link: Joins ITOM-015 or ITOM-031 to ITOM-076

rules.rule: Business Critical service whose impact calculation cannot return a result, traced to a specific ITOM cause
rules.what_it_means: A Business Critical service whose impact calculation cannot return a result, with the specific ITOM cause traced.
rules.why_it_matters: The single most persuasive finding available to you. It names a service the business cares about, states that impact analysis cannot work for it, and points at the exact ITOM defect responsible. It converts an abstract data quality conversation into an operational risk conversation.
rules.source_tables_fields: Service criticality, impact calculation results, CI reachability, and the ITOM findings affecting the CIs in its path
rules.detection_logic: Business Critical services with empty or truncated impact results, joined to the ITOM findings affecting the CIs at the break point
rules.threshold_parameter: Any Business Critical service with a structurally impossible impact result
rules.confidence_basis: 100% on the impact result. Cause attribution confidence from the strength of the linked ITOM finding.
rules.evidence_to_show: Service, criticality, incident volume, the traversal showing where the path breaks, the CIs at the break, and the ITOM finding responsible with its own evidence.
rules.false_positive_guard: Service deliberately outside the impact model.
rules.remediation_lane: Lane 3 — the remediation is the chain, not a single fix
rules.cross_domain_link: The headline finding of the assessment; summarises the entire chain

rules.rule: MID outage window correlating with a relationship deletion window
rules.what_it_means: A MID Server outage window correlates with a relationship deletion window.
rules.why_it_matters: When the MID goes down, discovery cannot confirm relationships, and reconciliation removes them. The graph degrades as a direct consequence of a MID outage, and nothing connects the two events.
